| `emphasis?` | `ActionEmphasis` | `"primary"` fills the button with the accent; keep one per dashboard, as more warn in development. Default: `"secondary"`. |
| `confirm?` | `ActionConfirm` | Ask for confirmation before running. |
| `form?` | `FieldDef<Input>[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `input`. |
| `inputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Input>` | Cross-field input validation for trusted action code. |
| `outputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Output>` | Required before arbitrary `data` may cross the client boundary. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Restrict the action to a role. Enforced before `run`. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `run` | `(input: Input, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>) => Promise<ActionResult<Output>>` | Server-side handler. Runs only after every guard has passed. |

Actions are secondary buttons, destructive ones in the error colour.
`emphasis: "primary"` fills one with the accent; more than one primary on a
dashboard warns in development.

```ts
dashboardAction({ key: "retry", label: "Retry failed runs", emphasis: "primary", run: retryFailed });
```

`hideActionsBar: true` on the dashboard hides the bar.

### DrawerAction

Rendered in the drawer's menu, like a row action, and takes the same options
except `hidden` and `disabled`. Its `form` is a list of fields, as on a row action.

`DrawerAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered beside the label. |
| `variant?` | `ActionVariant` | Button styling. |
| `placement?` | `"inline" \| "menu"` | `"inline"` renders a button in the row; `"menu"` puts it in the row menu. |
| `confirm?` | `ActionConfirm` | Ask for confirmation before running. |
| `form?` | `FieldDef<Input>[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `input`. |
| `inputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Input>` | Cross-field input validation for trusted action code. |
| `outputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Output>` | Required before arbitrary `data` may cross the client boundary. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Restrict the action to a role. Enforced before `run`. |
| `when?` | `(context: FieldWriteContext<Row>) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Offer and run the action only on rows where this holds; menus check it with no `input`, the route with it. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `run` | `(row: Row, input: Input, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>) => Promise<ActionResult<Output>>` | Server-side handler. Runs only after every guard has passed. |

### ActionResult

What every `run` returns.

`ActionResult`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `true` |  |
| `message?` | `string` | Toast shown to the operator. |
| `refresh?` | `boolean \| string \| string[]` | Revalidate after the action. `true` refreshes the current resource; a string publishes that one channel. |
| `redirect?` | `string` | Send the operator to this path once the action succeeds. |
| `download?` | `{ filename: string; data: string \| Blob \| Uint8Array; mime?: string }` | Hand the operator a generated file. |
| `filename` | `string` |  |
| `data` | `string \| Blob \| Uint8Array` |  |
| `mime?` | `string` |  |
| `data?` | `never` |  |
| `data?` | `Data` |  |
| `ok` | `false` |  |
| `error` | `string` | Message shown to the operator. Safe to display — never include internals. |
| `fieldErrors?` | `Record<string, string>` | Per-field messages, keyed by `FieldDef.name`, for actions with a `form`. |

`ActionInput` defaults to `Record<string, unknown>`. `{ ok: false, error }` shows
`error` to the operator as written. A thrown `FlowpanelError` keeps its status;
anything else becomes a `500` and goes to `hooks.onError`, or, without a hook, to one
`console.error` line with its request id.

### ActionContext

The last argument to every `run`.

`ActionContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unsafe?` | `{ db: Db }` | Explicit escape hatch for trusted action implementations. |
| `actorId` | `string \| null` | Caller identity — same derivation the audit trail uses (`auth.userId`, then `session.id`, then `session.user.id`). |
| `publish` | `(channel: string, payload?: unknown) => Promise<void>` | Push a realtime message to every connected admin. |

`ctx.unsafe.db` is the adapter's client, present only when the action declares `unsafe: ["db"]`. `ctx.publish` sends a realtime event.

### Validation

A `form` is validated on the server before `run`: `required`, then each field's
`validate`. A failure returns `422` with `fieldErrors`, one message per field.

## Drawer

Layout, tabs and actions of the row side panel.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/drawer

Documented types: DrawerConfig, DrawerTabFields, DrawerTabResource, DrawerTabWidgets, DrawerAction, DrawerPayload

A drawer shows one row over the list. Declare `drawer` on a resource; a row click
opens it unless `rowClick` says otherwise. Guide: [Record pages and drawers](/docs/build/detail-cards#drawer).

```ts
resource(orders, {
  columns: ["id", "customerEmail", "status"],
  rowClick: "drawer",
  drawer: {
    width: "xl",
    title: (row) => `Order ${row.id}`,
    tabs: [
      { key: "summary", label: "Summary", fields: "*" },
      { key: "items", label: "Items", resource: "order_items", filter: (row) => ({ orderId: row.id }) },
    ],
    actions: [
      {
        key: "refund",
        label: "Refund",
        variant: "destructive",
        access: "admin",
        confirm: "Refund this order?",
        form: [{ name: "reason", type: "textarea", required: true }],
        run: async (row, formData, ctx) => {
          await refund(db, row.id, formData.reason as string);
          return { ok: true, message: "Refunded", refresh: true };
        },
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

### DrawerConfig

`DrawerConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width?` | `DrawerWidth` | Panel width. Default: `"lg"`. |
| `title?` | `(row: Row) => string` | Panel title. Defaults to the row's key. |
| `subtitle?` | `(row: Row) => string` | The line under the title. Defaults to the resource's label. |
| `fields?` | `DrawerFieldList<Row>` | Fields shown when no `tabs` are declared. `"*"` shows every column. |
| `tabs?` | `DrawerTab<Row>[]` | Tabs to render instead of a flat field list. |
| `actions?` | `DrawerAction<Row>[]` | The row's own actions, in the header menu of the drawer and the record page. |

`DrawerWidth` is `"sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "full"`, defaulting to
`"lg"`.

With a `detail` page, the header links to it (`labels.drawer.viewDetails`). The
line under the title is the resource label unless you set `subtitle(row)`.

Without `tabs`, the drawer lists `fields` (`(keyof Row | FieldDef<Row>)[] | "*"`),
labelled and rendered by the matching columns. A `FieldDef.render` wins over the
column's; see [fields and sections](/docs/reference/resources#fields-and-sections).

#### Server-rendered cells

Renders in a drawer run concurrently on the server and become static HTML, so
return text or plain elements and use a pooled database client. A render that
returns a client component shows the list's cell or the formatted value instead.
A render that throws is logged as `[flowpanel] drawer render failed for "<field>"`
and the cell shows the formatted value.

### Tabs

`DrawerTab` is a union of three shapes, discriminated by which key you set.

#### DrawerTabFields

The row's own fields.

`DrawerTabFields`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier for the tab. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `fields` | `DrawerFieldList<Row>` | Fields to show. `"*"` shows every declared column. |

#### DrawerTabResource

Rows of a related resource, filtered by the open row.

`DrawerTabResource`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `resource` | `ResourceName` | Related resource to list. Must be registered on the same admin. |
| `filter?` | `(row: Row) => Record<string, unknown>` | Filter applied to the related resource, derived from the open row. |

The related resource's access rules apply; a tab the operator may not read is
empty. The tab shows the first 20 rows, with no pagination.

#### DrawerTabWidgets

Dashboard widgets, scoped to the open row.

`DrawerTabWidgets`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `widgets` | `Exclude< WidgetConfig, CustomWidget \| TimelineWidget \| HeatmapWidget \| ChecklistWidget \| TrackerWidget >[]` | `custom()`, `tracker()` and page-rendered widgets (`timeline`, `heatmap`, `checklist`) are not renderable here — the drawer serializes over the wire. |

`custom`, `timeline`, `heatmap`, `checklist` and `tracker` widgets are a type error
here, and the last four also fail at `defineAdmin`; use a record page tab. Each widget is serialized
before it reaches the browser:

```ts
type SerializedWidget =
  | { kind: "metric"; label: string; value: number | string; /* format, sublabel, tone, span, realtime */ }
  | { kind: "table"; rows: Record<string, unknown>[]; columns: { field: string; label?: string }[]; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "statGroup"; stats: { label: string; value: string | number | CardDate; /* … */ }[]; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "chart"; subkind: "area" | "bar" | "line" | "pie"; label: string; dataPoints: number; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "stat"; label: string; value: number | string | CardDate; /* format, hint, href, tone */ }
  | { kind: "kv"; items: { label: string; value: string | CardDate; /* tone, href, long, rest, more */ }[]; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "bars"; rows: { label: string; value: number; href?: string /* … */ }[]; emptyState: string; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "funnel"; steps: { label: string; value: number; href?: string }[]; emptyState: string; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "list"; rows: ListCardRow[]; more?: { label: string; href?: string }; emptyState: string; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "unsupported"; label?: string; reason: string; failed?: true; span?: number };
```

`CardDate` is `{ kind: "date"; iso: string }`, an instant the card renders in the
viewer's time zone. A widget whose query throws becomes
`{ kind: "unsupported", failed: true }` with a safe message. Drawer widgets are static: a metric shows no delta, link or
sparkline, and a table has no row links.

### Actions

The drawer's header holds the record's Edit button and one menu with the
resource's row actions, these drawer actions and Delete, the same menu the
record page shows. Each runs with the same guards as every action; see
[DrawerAction](/docs/reference/actions#draweraction). An action the operator cannot
run, or whose `when` rejects the open row, is left out, and a deleted row offers
only Restore. `placement: "inline"` keeps an action as a button beside Edit, for
the one a reviewer clicks on every row.

`DrawerAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered beside the label. |
| `variant?` | `ActionVariant` | Button styling. |
| `placement?` | `"inline" \| "menu"` | `"inline"` renders a button in the row; `"menu"` puts it in the row menu. |
| `confirm?` | `ActionConfirm` | Ask for confirmation before running. |
| `form?` | `FieldDef<Input>[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `input`. |
| `inputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Input>` | Cross-field input validation for trusted action code. |
| `outputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Output>` | Required before arbitrary `data` may cross the client boundary. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Restrict the action to a role. Enforced before `run`. |
| `when?` | `(context: FieldWriteContext<Row>) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Offer and run the action only on rows where this holds; menus check it with no `input`, the route with it. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `run` | `(row: Row, input: Input, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>) => Promise<ActionResult<Output>>` | Server-side handler. Runs only after every guard has passed. |

### The payload

What `GET /api/flowpanel/drawer/<resource>/<id>` returns.

`DrawerPayload`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | `Record<string, unknown>` |  |
| `title` | `string` |  |
| `subtitle?` | `string` | The line under the title, from `drawer.subtitle`. |
| `resourceLabel` | `string` | The resource's display label, so the drawer never shows the raw registry name. |
| `width` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "2xl" \| "full"` |  |
| `fields` | `SerializedFieldList` |  |
| `tabs` | `SerializedDrawerTab[] \| null` |  |
| `actions` | `SerializedDrawerAction[]` |  |
| `prerendered` | `Record<string, string>` | Field → HTML for fields whose column declares a `render`. |
| `labels` | `Record<string, string>` | Field → column label, so drawer rows read like their table headers. |
| `formats` | `Record<string, ColumnFormat>` | Field → column `format`. Plain data, rendered client-side exactly as the table does. |
| `references` | `Record<string, { label: string; href: string }>` | Field → the record a `reference` column points at, so a drawer opened from a link reads like one opened from its row. |
| `detailHref` | `string \| null` | The record's own page, when the resource configures `detail`. |
| `deleted` | `boolean` | Soft-deleted, shown only to a caller who could restore it. |
| `deletedTitle?` | `string` | The notice over a deleted row: "This customer was deleted". |
| `restorable` | `boolean` | A deleted row whose resource takes updates, so Restore can bring it back. |

### What crosses to the client

Only declared columns and fields, never the raw row. Rendered columns arrive as
HTML.

## Widgets

Every widget builder and the options it accepts.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/widgets

Documented types: WidgetContext, WidgetFormat, CaptionOptions, Freshness, Threshold, ResourceLink, DashboardLink, metric, MetricOptions, MetricResult, MetricDelta, table, TableWidgetOptions, WidgetColumn, statGroup, StatGroupOptions, StatItem, stat, StatOptions, StatResult, kv, KvOptions, KvItem, KvResult, bars, BarsOptions, BarRow, funnel, FunnelOptions, FunnelStep, list, ListOptions, banner, ListRow, tracker, TrackerOptions, TrackerRow, timeline, TimelineOptions, TimelineSource, TimelineEvent, TimelinePage, heatmap, HeatmapOptions, HeatmapSource, checklist, ChecklistOptions, ChecklistItem, filled, custom, CustomOptions, ChartOptionsBase, areaChart, AreaChartOptions, barChart, BarChartOptions, lineChart, LineChartOptions, pieChart, PieChartOptions, series, SeriesOptions, breakdown, BreakdownOptions, presetRange, previousRange, fillDays, dashboard, page, DashboardConfig, SectionConfig, DateRangeConfig, DashboardFilter, ResolvedDateRange, WidgetDateRange, PageConfig

Widgets fill dashboard sections, record page tabs and drawer tabs. Each builder
returns a `WidgetConfig`; every `query` runs on the server with a `WidgetContext`.
On a record page or in a drawer, `ctx.row` is the record. A drawer renders
[static cards](/docs/reference/drawer#drawertabwidgets).

```ts
import { areaChart, dashboard, metric, statGroup, table } from "@flowpanel/kit";

export const overview = dashboard({
  path: "/",
  label: "Overview",
  dateRange: { preset: "last30d" },
  sections: [
    {
      label: "Revenue",
      widgets: [
        metric("MRR", async ({ db, dateRange }) => mrr(db, dateRange), {
          format: "currency",
          span: 3,
          drilldown: { resource: "invoices" },
        }),
        areaChart("Revenue over time", async ({ db }) => revenueSeries(db), {
          x: "day",
          y: ["subscriptions", "one-off"],
          stacked: true,
          span: 9,
        }),
      ],
    },
  ],
});
```

### WidgetContext

What every widget `query` receives.

`WidgetContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `db` | `DB` | Your database client, exactly as handed to the adapter. |
| `session` | `Session \| null` |  |
| `role` | `string` | The signed-in role, as `auth.role` returns it. |
| `dateRange` | `WidgetDateRange` | The picked range, the period before it and the admin's zone, resolved to dates. |
| `filters` | `Readonly<Record<string, string>>` | The dashboard's active filters by key; `{}` on a record page or with none set. Bind them as parameters. |
| `req` | `Request` |  |
| `row?` | `Record<string, unknown>` | Row of the record being viewed when the widget sits in a detail tab. |
| `id?` | `string` | The viewed record's key as a string — `row[rowKey]`. Absent on a dashboard, or when the key is not a string or number. |
| `link` | `(target: LinkTarget) => string` | Resolve a link target to an href, for the props of a custom widget. |
| `query` | `{ <T>(key: string, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>; <A extends unknown[], T>(fn: (...args: A) => Promise<T>, ...args: A): Promise<T>; <T>(fn: (ctx: WidgetContext<DB>) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>; }` | Memoises a query per request: a key and a thunk, or a function and its arguments. A function passed alone that declares a parameter is called with this context: `query(hourly)` runs `hourly(ctx)`. |
| `labels` | `ResolvedLabels` | The admin's resolved chrome strings, so a widget never hard-codes English. |
| `format` | `WidgetFormat` | The admin's formatters — locale, zone and currency from `formatting`. |
| `sql` | `<Row = Record<string, unknown>>( strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[] ) => Promise<Row[]>` | One read-only statement, as a tagged template; every interpolated value binds as a parameter, never as text. Runs exactly the statement you write — no tenant scope, access rule or soft-delete filter applied; `count`/reads do. |
| `count` | `<N extends ResourceName>( resource: N, where?: Where<RowOf<N>>, options?: CountOptions<RowOf<N>>, ) => Promise<number>` | How many rows of a registered resource match `where`, under the same role, access and scope checks as its list. Memoised per request by resource, `where` and range; a resource the session may not read counts `0`. |
| `read` | `<N extends ResourceName>( resource: N, options?: ReadOptions<RowOf<N>>, ) => Promise<RowOf<N>[]>` | Rows of a registered resource under the same role, access, scope, field and soft-delete rules as its list. Memoised per request by resource and options; a resource the session may not read returns `[]`. |
| `rowOf` | `<N extends ResourceName>(resource: N) => RowOf<N>` | The record this card shows, typed by its resource. Throws on a dashboard, which has no record, and on another resource's card; the message names both. |

`link` turns a named target into an href under `paths.admin`:
`link({ resource: "orders" })` is the list, `{ resource: "orders", id }` one record,
and `{ filter: { status: "paid" } }` adds `?f_status=paid`. Where an option takes a
link, pass the target itself.

`query` memoises for the request, so widgets that ask the same question run it
once. Pass a key and a thunk, `query("mrr", () => mrr(db))`, or a function and its
arguments, `query(mrr, db, ctx.dateRange)`; arguments key by value (objects by
identity). A failure is shared too. Use a function declared once: an inline one is
new on every call and never shares. A function passed alone that declares a
parameter receives the context, so `query(hourly)` runs `hourly(ctx)` once; a
function whose parameters are all defaulted is called with none. The `compare`
period runs it again with its own range.

`count` is memoised the same way: one resource and `where`, written in any key
order, count once per request. `id` is the viewed record's key as a string, read
through the resource's `rowKey`; a dashboard widget has none.

`dateRange` is the picked range with `previous` and `timeZone`. For `today`,
`yesterday`, `MTD`, `QTD` and `YTD`, `previous` is the same stretch one period back
at the same clock time; for `last7d`, `last30d` and a custom range it is the span
of the same length before. Over a record's whole history it is `null`.

`filters` holds the dashboard's active filters by key, `{ platform: "kwork" }` for
`?f_platform=kwork`, and is `{}` when none is set. Bind it in your own query.

`labels` is the resolved `LabelsConfig`. `row` is set on a record page.

```ts
metric("Paid orders", async (ctx) => ({
  value: await ctx.query("paid-orders", () => countPaid(ctx.db, ctx.dateRange)),
  href: { resource: "orders", filter: { status: "paid" } },
}));
```

#### WidgetFormat

`WidgetFormat`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | `(value: MomentInput) => string` | The calendar day in the admin's zone; a `YYYY-MM-DD` string is that day. |
| `dateTime` | `(value: MomentInput) => string` | Day and clock, as a table cell shows a timestamp. |
| `relative` | `(value: MomentInput, now?: Date) => string` | How long ago — `5 minutes ago`, `yesterday`. `now` defaults to the current time. |
| `number` | `(value: NumberInput, digits?: number) => string` | A number with the locale's grouping and at most `digits` decimals. |
| `money` | `(value: NumberInput, options?: { currency?: string; digits?: number; minorUnits?: number }) => string` | An amount, in minor units when `minorUnits` is set, in `currency` (default `formatting.currency`), `digits` decimals (0). |
| `percent` | `(value: NumberInput, digits?: number) => string` | A fraction as a percentage — `0.42` is `42%`. |
| `duration` | `(ms: NumberInput) => string` | Milliseconds as the largest units that fit — `2 hr 5 min`. |
| `plural` | `(count: number, label: string \| PluralLabel) => string` | A count in the plural form the locale picks; `{n}` is the formatted count. |

`ctx.format` formats with the admin's `locale`, `timeZone` and `currency`, the same
way table cells do.

```ts
stat("Latency", async (ctx) => {
  const s = await ctx.query(latencyStages, ctx.db, ctx.dateRange);
  return {
    value: ctx.format.duration(s.p50Ms),
    hint: `p95 ${ctx.format.duration(s.p95Ms)} · ${ctx.format.plural(s.n, { one: "{n} order", other: "{n} orders" })}`,
  };
});
```

### Shared option types

`Span` is a whole number from `1` to `12`. A section without `columns` uses 12
columns once a widget sets `span`. On a phone every widget takes the full row.

`NumericFormat` is `"number" | "currency" | "percent" | "bytes" | "duration"`.

`Tone` is `"default" | "accent" | "ok" | "warn" | "err" | "info" | "muted"`.

Every widget and dashboard accepts `realtime`: a channel name, `{ resource: "orders" }`,
or a list of them. When one fires, only that widget re-runs.

Every widget accepts `access`, the same rule a dashboard or action takes: a role, a
list of roles, or a function. A widget the caller's role is refused is left out of
the dashboard, record page or drawer, and its queries never run. A section left
with no widget is left out too. `ctx.role` gives a query the caller's role.

```ts
metric("MRR", (ctx) => mrr(ctx.db, ctx.dateRange), { format: "currency", access: "admin" });
```

`maxRange`, such as `"30d"`, is for rows your app deletes after that long. The
widget queries from `max(from, to − N, now − N)` and says so in its caption; a
range that ended before `now − N` runs no query and shows `—`. `heatmap` and
`tracker` do not take it.

#### Captions

A card shows at most one caption under its title, in this order of precedence:
1. the expired state;
2. where `maxRange` cut the range;
3. `freshness`: when the data was last written, in the warn tone with a ▲ past
   `warnAfter`;
4. `coverage`: a note that the data is a sample.

A failing `freshness.at` is logged and skipped.

`CaptionOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Who sees the widget. A refused widget is left out of the page and its queries never run. |
| `freshness?` | `Freshness` | Say under the title how old the data is. |
| `coverage?` | `string` | Say under the title that the data is a sample, e.g. "users who accepted analytics". |

`Freshness`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<Date \| null>` | When the data was last written, e.g. the newest rollup row; `null` when unknown. |
| `warnAfter?` | ``${number}m` \| `${number}h` \| `${number}d`` | Older than this shows in the warn tone with a ▲. |

```ts
metric("Runs today", runsToday, {
  freshness: { at: async (c) => lastRollupHour(c), warnAfter: "2h" },
});
metric("With analytics consent", consentShare, {
  format: "percent",
  coverage: "users who accepted analytics",
});
```

### Thresholds

`Threshold`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `warn` | `number` | The value at which it is a warning. |
| `err` | `number` | The value at which it is an error. |
| `goodWhen?` | `GoodWhen` | Which direction is good. Left out, the numbers say it: `warn` below `err` means higher is worse, and reverse. Given, it must agree with them, or `defineAdmin` throws. |
| `min?` | `number` | Below this many observations the value is `muted`: too few to judge. |

Pass one threshold as `tones` to `metric`, `stat`, `bars`, `tracker` and the
`number`, `percent` and `duration` column formats. The tone is `ok`, `warn` or `err`,
and `muted` below `min` observations (a metric or stat returns them as `volume`).
An explicit `tone` wins. `toneFor(value, threshold, volume)` gives the same answer
in your own code.

`warn` below `err` means higher is worse; `warn` above `err` means lower is worse.
A `goodWhen` that contradicts the numbers makes `defineAdmin` throw.

```ts
import { type Threshold, metric, resource, toneFor } from "@flowpanel/kit";

const ERRORS: Threshold = { warn: 0.3, err: 0.5, min: 20 };

metric(
  "Run errors",
  async (c) => {
    const { rate, runs } = await runErrorRate(c);
    return { value: rate, volume: runs };
  },
  { format: "percent", tones: ERRORS },
);
resource(schema.monitors, { columns: [{ field: "errorRate", format: { kind: "percent", tones: ERRORS } }] });
toneFor(0.42, ERRORS, 120); // "warn": 120 runs, above warn and below err
```

### Links

A widget link names its target instead of spelling a path.

`ResourceLink`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | `N` |  |
| `id?` | `string \| number` | One record's page instead of the list. |
| `filter?` | `true extends ManyNames<N> ? Record<string, unknown> : ListFilters<RowOf<N>>` | List filters keyed by the target's fields: a value, `{ gte, lte }` or an array, written as the list's own `f_<field>` URL keys. Any keys while the link does not name one resource. |
| `view?` | `string` | A view from the resource's `views`, applied by name before `filter`. |
| `tab?` | `string` | A detail tab, with `id`. |
| `range?` | `true extends ManyNames<N> ? string : keyof RowOf<N> & string` | A `daterange` filter field that receives the widget's range, bound for bound. |

`DashboardLink`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dashboard` | `string` |  |
| `range?` | `boolean` | Carry the widget's range: the preset, or `from`/`to` for a custom range. A resource link names the `daterange` field instead. Default: `true`. |
| `filter?` | `Record<string, string>` | Dashboard filters the link sets, by key; a link carries no filter implicitly. |

A `LinkTarget` is a string (used as written), a `ResourceLink` or a `DashboardLink`.

- `{ resource: "order" }` is the list, `{ resource: "order", id }` one record, and `tab`
  a record tab.
- `filter` becomes the list's `f_<field>` keys, or a dashboard's declared filters. A
  `Date` is written as its day, `{ gte, lte }` as a range, an array as `a,b`. A key
  the target does not declare fails at `defineAdmin`.
- `view` applies one of the resource's saved `views`.
- `range` on a resource link names the `daterange` filter that receives the widget's
  range, so the list shows exactly the counted rows.
- `{ dashboard: "/system" }` is a dashboard or page by `path`. It carries the widget's
  range unless `range: false`.

An unregistered resource, view or dashboard throws and lists the registered ones.

`ctx.link(target)` resolves the same targets to a string, for the props of a custom
widget:

```ts
custom(PlatformGrid, async (ctx) => ({
  platforms: (await platforms(ctx.db)).map((p) => ({
    ...p,
    runsHref: ctx.link({ resource: "scraper_run", filter: { platform: p.key }, range: "startedAt" }),
  })),
}));
```

Every widget link option takes a `LinkTarget`, or a function of the context that
returns one or `null`.

### metric

`MetricOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon?` | `string` | Rendered as-is next to the label. Any string — an emoji, a ligature. No icon-name lookup exists. |
| `format?` | `NumericFormat` | How the number is rendered. |
| `sublabel?` | `string` | Small caption under the value. |
| `delta?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<MetricDelta \| null>` | Period-over-period change, queried alongside the value. |
| `compare?` | `boolean \| { against?: "previous" \| "weekAgo" }` | Query the compared period too and show the change: `previous`, or `against: "weekAgo"` for the same range seven days back. Needs a numeric value; a `delta` the query returns wins. |
| `goodWhen?` | `"up" \| "down" \| "neutral"` | Which direction is good news; colours the change ("neutral" doesn't), and `tones` must agree with it. Default: `"up"`. |
| `sparkline?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<number[]>` | Trend line drawn inside the card. |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | Semantic color of the value. |
| `tones?` | `Threshold` | Tone the value against a threshold; an explicit `tone` wins. |
| `drilldown?` | `Link` | Turns the whole card into a link — a path, a named target, or one computed from the context. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |

A metric's `icon` is rendered as given, such as an emoji; it is not an `IconName`.

A query returns a number, a string, or a `MetricResult`, whose fields win over the
matching options.

A metric that counts rows takes `{ count, where, range }` instead of a query. Its
value is `ctx.count(count, where, { range })`, and it links to exactly the rows it
counted unless you set `drilldown`. A missing `where` value counts `0` with no link.

```ts
metric("Visits", { count: "user_visit", where: (c) => ({ userId: c.id }), range: "startedAt" }, {
  compare: true,
});
metric("Sign-ups", { count: "user", range: "createdAt" }, { compare: true });
```

`where` may be a function of the context. Its fields must be columns or filters of
the counted list, and `range` one of its `daterange` filters; `defineAdmin` checks
both. `drilldown: () => null` removes the link.

`compare: true` runs the query again with `ctx.dateRange.previous` and shows the
change; `compare: { against: "weekAgo" }` compares with the same range seven days
earlier. Set `goodWhen: "down"` for costs and errors. A `delta` from the query wins.
A value that was 0 in the earlier period reads "new" beside "was 0", since a
percentage of nothing means nothing; 0 both times reads "No change".

```ts
metric("New users", async (ctx) => countSignups(ctx.db, ctx.dateRange), { compare: true });
```

#### MetricResult

`MetricResult`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number \| string` |  |
| `tone?` | `Tone` |  |
| `sublabel?` | `string` |  |
| `delta?` | `MetricDelta` |  |
| `href?` | `LinkTarget` | Turns the whole card into a link — a path or a named target. |
| `volume?` | `number` | Observations behind the value, compared with `tones.min`. |

#### MetricDelta

`MetricDelta`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | Fractional change — `0.12` renders as +12%. Inside ±1% the card shows no direction. |
| `vs` | `string` | What the comparison is against, e.g. `"prior period"`. |
| `previous?` | `number` | The value compared against, shown muted beside the change. A count under 20 shows the absolute change (`+3`); a `percent` metric shows percentage points (`+3 pp`). |

The change prints signed (`+12%`, `−3`). Inside ±1 % it has no sign, and only a
change of 5 % or more is coloured. With `previous` set, the old value shows beside
it. A count whose `previous` is under 20 shows the absolute change, and a
`format: "percent"` metric its change in points (`+3 pp`). `goodWhen: "down"`
colours a fall as good; `"neutral"` never colours.

### table

Point it at a `resource` to reuse its columns, or pass your own `query` and
`columns`, which are checked against the query's row type. On the `resource`
path a bare key keeps the resource's header and format; an object overrides them.

`TableWidgetOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `filterOnClick?` | `string` | A dashboard filter key: clicking a row sets it to the row's `rowKey` value on the current dashboard. |
| `resource?` | `ResourceName` | Registered resource to pull rows and columns from. |
| `query?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<R[]>` | Supply rows yourself instead of reading a resource. |
| `where?` | `Record<string, unknown> \| ((ctx: WidgetContext) => Record<string, unknown>)` | Narrow the `resource` read: a filter keyed by its fields, or one computed from the context — `(c) => ({ userId: c.id })`. A missing value throws instead of reading every row. |
| `range?` | `string` | A timestamp field of `resource` that the picked range bounds, as `ResourceLink.range` does. |
| `columns?` | `Array<RowKey<R> \| WidgetColumn<R>>` | Columns to show, defaulting to the resource's own list columns; give an object to name/format a query-produced column. |
| `rowKey?` | `RowKey<R>` | Which field identifies a row. Defaults to the resource's own key, and to `"id"` for a `query`. A row without one renders but is never acted on. |
| `rowHref?` | `(row: R, ctx: WidgetContext) => LinkTarget \| null` | Turn each row into a link — a path or a named target. Return `null` to leave a row inert. |
| `seeAll?` | `boolean \| Link` | Link the card heading. `true` links the `resource`'s own list; a `Link` names any target, and a string is used as written. |
| `limit?` | `number` | Row cap. An explicit value caps both paths; the default applies only to the `resource` read. Default: `10`. |
| `emptyState?` | `ReactNode` | Rendered in place of the table body when there are zero rows. |
| `density?` | `"comfortable" \| "compact"` | Row height: `"compact"` sets 40px rows for a card that lists a few. Default: `"comfortable"`. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |

#### WidgetColumn

`WidgetColumn`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `RowKey<R>` |  |
| `label?` | `string` |  |
| `format?` | `ColumnFormat` |  |
| `align?` | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"` |  |
| `width?` | `number \| string` |  |

`rowKey` defaults to the resource's key, or `"id"` for a `query`. `rowHref` links
each row (`null` for none); `seeAll: true` links the heading to the list. `limit`
defaults to 10 on the `resource` path. `density: "compact"` sets 40 px rows.

`where` narrows the `resource` read with [`ctx.read` values](/docs/reference/contexts#where-values),
or a function such as `(c) => ({ userId: c.id })`. `range` names the timestamp the
picked range bounds: `table({ resource: "user", range: "createdAt" })`.

```ts
table({
  resource: "orders",
  label: "Recent orders",
  columns: ["id", { field: "total", label: "Total", format: "money", align: "right" }],
  rowHref: (row) => ({ resource: "orders", id: row.id }),
  seeAll: true,
  limit: 5,
});
```

### statGroup

`StatGroupOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `stats` | `StatItem[]` | Rows of the group, in order. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |

#### StatItem

`StatItem`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `value` | `StatValue \| ((ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<StatValue \| KvResult>)` | A literal, or a function resolved per request that may return a `KvResult`. The record, in a detail tab, is `ctx.row`. |
| `format?` | `NumericFormat` |  |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | Semantic color of the value. |

`StatValue` is `string | number | boolean | bigint | Date | null | undefined`; a
`Date` is formatted like a table cell. A resolver may return a [`KvResult`](#kvresult)
with its own tone and link.

```ts
statGroup({
  label: "Account",
  span: 6,
  stats: [
    { label: "Plan", value: async (ctx) => planOf(ctx.row) },
    { label: "Joined", value: async (ctx) => joinedAt(ctx.row) },
    { label: "Open invoices", value: async (ctx) => ctx.count("invoices", { status: "open" }) },
  ],
});
```

### Cards

Small cards take values and labels, format them with the admin's `formatting`,
and colour items by `tone`.

#### stat

One number with a label, without `metric()`'s delta and sparkline.

`StatOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hint?` | `string` | Small caption under the value. |
| `href?` | `Link` | Turns the whole card into a link — a path, a named target, or one computed from the context. |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | Semantic color of the value. |
| `tones?` | `Threshold` | Tone the value against a threshold; an explicit `tone` wins. |
| `goodWhen?` | `GoodWhen` | Which direction is good news; `tones` must agree with it. Default: `"up"`. |
| `format?` | `NumericFormat` | How a numeric value is rendered. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |

##### StatResult

A resolver may return a `StatResult`, whose fields win over the options.

`StatResult`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `StatValue` |  |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | Semantic color of the value. |
| `hint?` | `string` | Small caption under the value. |
| `href?` | `LinkTarget` | Turns the whole card into a link — a path or a named target. |
| `volume?` | `number` | Observations behind the value, compared with `tones.min`. |

```ts
stat("Open invoices", async (ctx) => {
  const filter = { customerId: ctx.rowOf("customers").id, status: "open" } as const;
  const value = await ctx.count("invoices", filter);
  return { value, href: { resource: "invoices", filter }, tone: value > 0 ? "warn" : "ok" };
});
```

#### kv

Facts about one thing. An item's `format` takes a `ColumnFormat` or `NumericFormat`.
An item with `field` reads the card's `record`, which runs once and defaults to the
viewed row on a record page:

```ts
kv({
  label: "Feed filters",
  record: (c) => c.read("freelancer_profile", { where: { userId: c.id }, limit: 1 }).then((r) => r[0]),
  items: [{ label: "Rate", field: "hourlyRate", format: "number" }],
});
```

An item with `long` is a paragraph; past `lines` lines (6 by default) the rest
folds under "Show all". `empty` replaces "—" for a missing value.

```ts
kv({
  label: "Texts",
  columns: 1,
  record: profileOf,
  items: [
    { label: "About", field: "bio", long: true, empty: "Not filled" },
    { label: "Resume", field: "resumeText", long: { lines: 10 }, empty: "Not uploaded" },
  ],
});
```

`KvOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `items` | `KvItem<R>[]` | Rows of the card, in order. |
| `record?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => R \| null \| undefined \| Promise<R \| null \| undefined>` | The record `field` items read, resolved once per card. Omitted: the viewed record on a record page, and nothing on a dashboard. |
| `columns?` | `1 \| 2` | Rows per grid line. Default: `2`. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |

##### KvItem

`KvItem`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `value?` | `StatValue \| ((ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<StatValue \| KvResult>)` | A literal, or a function resolved per request that may return a `KvResult`. Omit it with `field`. |
| `field?` | `keyof R & string` | A field of the card's `record` — the viewed row by default — shown instead of `value`. |
| `format?` | `ColumnFormat \| NumericFormat` |  |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | Semantic color of the value. |
| `href?` | `Link` | Renders the value as a link — a path, a named target, or one computed from the context. |
| `long?` | `boolean \| { lines?: number }` | A paragraph across the card, line breaks kept; past `lines` lines the rest folds under "Show all". Default: `false; `lines` defaults to 6`. |
| `empty?` | `string` | Printed instead of "—" when the value is missing or blank. |

##### KvResult

An item resolver may return a `KvResult`, whose `tone` and `href` win over the
item's. `statGroup` items take the same result.

`KvResult`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `StatValue` |  |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | Semantic color of the value. |
| `href?` | `LinkTarget` | Renders the value as a link — a path or a named target. |

```ts
kv({
  items: [
    {
      label: "Failed runs",
      value: async (ctx) => {
        const value = await ctx.count("runs", { status: "failed" });
        return { value, tone: value > 0 ? "err" : "ok", href: { resource: "runs" } };
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

#### bars

A ranked breakdown, sized against the largest value or `max`. Set `max` for a
rate:

```ts
bars({ label: "Win rate by budget", query: async (ctx) => winRates(ctx.db), format: "percent", max: 1 });
```

`BarsOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `filterOnClick?` | `string` | A dashboard filter key: clicking a bar sets it to the row's `key` on the current dashboard. |
| `query` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<BarRow[]>` |  |
| `format?` | `NumericFormat` | How bar values are rendered. |
| `max?` | `number` | The value a full bar stands for — `1` for a rate with `format: "percent"`. Default, and for a value of `0` or less: the largest value in the rows. |
| `share?` | `boolean` | Show each row's part of the total beside its value: its own `share`, else of the rows' sum. |
| `goodWhen?` | `"up" \| "down" \| "neutral"` | Which direction is good news; colours each row's change ("neutral" doesn't), and `tones` must agree with it. Default: `"up"`. |
| `tones?` | `Threshold` | Tone each bar against a threshold by its value; a row's own `tone` wins. |
| `compare?` | `boolean \| { against?: "previous" \| "weekAgo" }` | Runs the query for the compared period too and fills each row's `previous`, joined by `key` then `label`. No change shows past `maxRange` or over a whole history. |
| `emptyState?` | `ReactNode` | Shown instead of the bars when the query returns nothing. Text or any node; the drawer shows only text. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |

`share: true` shows each row's share of the total; a top-N query returns each
row's `share` itself. A row's `previous` shows its change with the `MetricDelta`
rules.

`compare: true` (or `{ against: "weekAgo" }`) runs the query for the earlier period
and fills each row's `previous`, joining by `key`, else `label`. A row the earlier
period lacks counts as 0 there, unless those rows fold the rest into "Other", where
it shows no change. A row that grew from 0 reads "new" instead of a percentage, and
a row at 0 both times shows no change. A query with a `LIMIT` of its own should fold
the rest with `breakdown({ top })`, or a row that was just outside it reads "new". With `top`, pass the earlier
rows to `breakdown({ previous })` instead.

```ts
bars({
  label: "New orders by marketplace",
  share: true,
  compare: true,
  query: async (c) => breakdown(await c.query(hourly), { by: "platform", value: "orders", keys: PLATFORMS }),
});
```

##### BarRow

`BarRow`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key?` | `string` | Stable identity: `compare` joins the previous period by it, and a filter sets it. `breakdown()` fills it. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `value` | `number` |  |
| `href?` | `LinkTarget` | Links the bar's label — a path or a named target. |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | Fill color of the bar. |
| `previous?` | `number` | The same row's value in the period before; the card marks the change. |
| `share?` | `number` | This row's part of the real total, 0 to 1, for a top-N query; shown with `share`. |

#### funnel

Stages in order, from counts. The card shows each step's share of the first and
its drop-off. With `alertDrop`, the largest drop-off is marked `warn` when it loses
more than that share of the step before.

`FunnelOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `query` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<FunnelStep[]>` |  |
| `format?` | `NumericFormat` | How step values are rendered. |
| `alertDrop?` | `number` | Share lost from the step before, as a fraction, past which the step with the largest drop is marked with the `warn` tone. Unset, no step is toned. |
| `emptyState?` | `ReactNode` | Shown instead of the steps when the query returns nothing. Text or any node; the drawer shows only text. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |

##### FunnelStep

`FunnelStep`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `value` | `number` |  |
| `href?` | `LinkTarget` | Links the step's label — a path or a named target. |

#### list

A short feed, such as latest signups or failing jobs.

`ListOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `query` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<ListRow[]>` |  |
| `emptyState?` | `ReactNode` | Shown instead of the lines when the query returns nothing. Text or any node; the drawer shows only text. |
| `variant?` | `"list" \| "banner"` | `"banner"`: a strip tinted by the worst row, ordered err → warn → info; with no rows it shows `allClear`. Default: `"list"`. |
| `limit?` | `number` | Rows shown; the rest become one "N more" line. |
| `more?` | `Link` | Where the "N more" line leads. |
| `allClear?` | `string` | A banner's line when there are no rows. Default: `labels.widget.allClear`. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |

A row can carry `count` and `since` (printed relative). `limit` folds the rest into
an "N more" line linking to `more`.

##### banner

`list({ variant: "banner", span: 12 })`: rows ordered err, warn, info, then by
`count`. The first row is a sentence, the rest are lines. With no rows it shows
`allClear`.

```ts
banner({ query: priorities, limit: 3, more: { dashboard: "/system" }, allClear: "Nothing on fire" });
```

##### ListRow

`ListRow`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key?` | `string` | Stable identity for the row, such as a record id. Default: its position. |
| `text` | `string` |  |
| `meta?` | `string` | Trailing detail — a timestamp, a count, an owner. |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | A leading dot in this color; `warn` and `err` also color the text. |
| `href?` | `LinkTarget` | Links the line's text — a path or a named target. |
| `count?` | `number` | Impact, shown right-aligned in the admin's locale: "37". |
| `since?` | `Date \| string` | When it started, shown relative in the admin's locale: "3 hours ago". |

Set `key` when realtime updates reorder rows.

```ts
import { bars, funnel, kv, list, stat } from "@flowpanel/kit";

const widgets = [
  stat("Active trials", async (ctx) => countTrials(ctx.db), { hint: "ends within 7 days" }),
  kv({
    label: "This account",
    items: [
      { label: "Plan", value: "Pro" },
      { label: "Balance", value: async (ctx) => balance(ctx.db), format: "money" },
    ],
  }),
  bars({ label: "Revenue by plan", query: async (ctx) => revenueByPlan(ctx.db), format: "currency" }),
  funnel({ label: "Signup", query: async (ctx) => signupSteps(ctx.db) }),
  list({ label: "Latest signups", query: async (ctx) => latestSignups(ctx.db) }),
];
```

#### tracker

One row per key and one block per hour of a window ending now, regardless of the
date picker. The window is 24 hours by default; past 48 hours the blocks are days.

The query receives the window as `ctx.dateRange`. `at` places rows in blocks, `by`
makes the rows, and `value` and `volume` fold each block like `series()`. `tones`
colours blocks; a row's dot is the worst of its last three. `rows` takes prebuilt
rows instead. Not available in drawers.

`TrackerOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `filterOnClick?` | `string` | A dashboard filter key: clicking a row sets it to the row's key on the current dashboard. |
| `query?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<R[]>` | Rows over the window: `ctx.dateRange` is the window, not the picked range. |
| `at?` | `keyof R & string` | The timestamp or `YYYY-MM-DD` field that places a row in a block. |
| `by?` | `keyof R & string` | One tracker row per value of this field. |
| `keys?` | `readonly string[]` | Values of `by` always shown, in this order. |
| `labels?` | `KeyLabels` | Row names per value of `by`: a map, an `enumOf()` or a function. |
| `value?` | `Fold<R>` | A block's number: a field to sum or a function of its rows. Default: the row count. |
| `volume?` | `Fold<R>` | Observations behind a block, compared with `tones.min`. Default: the row count. |
| `tones?` | `Threshold` | Tone each block by its value; without it a block with data is `accent`. |
| `goodWhen?` | `GoodWhen` | Which direction is good news; `tones` must agree with it. Default: `"up"`. |
| `format?` | `NumericFormat` | How a block's value prints in its hover title. |
| `rows?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<TrackerRow[]>` | Rows you built yourself, instead of `query`, `at` and `by`. |
| `window?` | ``${number}h` \| `${number}d`` | A window ending now, independent of the date picker: hourly blocks up to 48 hours, daily beyond. Default: `"24h"`. |
| `summary?` | `(row: TrackerRowResult, ctx: WidgetContext) => string \| Promise<string>` | Right-hand text per row, e.g. the last success; may query. |
| `rowHref?` | `(key: string, ctx: WidgetContext) => LinkTarget \| null` | Where a row's label leads. |
| `emptyState?` | `ReactNode` | Shown instead of the rows when there are none. Text or any node. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |

```ts
tracker({
  label: "Marketplaces · 24 h",
  query: hourly,
  at: "at",
  by: "platform",
  labels: Platform,
  value: errorRate,
  volume: "runs",
  tones: { warn: 0.3, err: 0.5, min: 20 },
  format: "percent",
  summary: async (row, c) => lastSuccess(await c.query(platformHealth), row.key, c.format),
  span: 12,
});
```

##### TrackerRow

`TrackerRow`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `cells` | `TrackerCell[]` |  |
| `summary?` | `string` | Right-hand text. |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | Default: the worst tone of the last three blocks. |
| `href?` | `LinkTarget` | Where the row's label leads. |

### timeline

Events newest first, grouped by day. Consecutive events of one kind with the same
`fold` key collapse into one line. A chip per kind (`kinds`) filters, and "Older"
pages back, under `?<id>.kind=` and `?<id>.before=`; `id` defaults to the tab key.

`query(ctx, page)` returns events that are not resource rows: at or before
`page.before`, at most `page.limit`, of `page.kinds` when set.

```ts
timeline({
  label: "Activity",
  kinds: Activity,
  query: async (ctx, page) => loadEvents(ctx.db, ctx.id, page),
});
```

On a record page a timeline covers the whole history, ignoring `detail.dateRange`.
Not available in drawers.

`TimelineOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `kinds` | `EnumDef \| Record<string, EnumEntry>` | The kinds — a chip each, with its label and tone. An `enumOf` works as is. |
| `query?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext, page: TimelinePage) => Promise<TimelineEvent[]>` | Events that are not rows of a resource. |
| `sources?` | `TimelineSource[]` | Resources read as events, merged with `query` by time; build each with `timeline.source`. |
| `group?` | `"day" \| false` | Group lines under days of the admin's zone; `false` for one list. Default: `"day"`. |
| `pageSize?` | `number` | Events per page, from 1 to 200. Default: `50`. |
| `id?` | `string` | The URL namespace of the chips and the paging, `?<id>.kind=` and `?<id>.before=`; unique per page. Default: `the detail tab's key, else "timeline", "timeline-2", … in page order`. |
| `emptyState?` | `ReactNode` | Shown instead of the lines when nothing happened. Text or any node. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |

#### Sources

`timeline.source(resource, source)` reads a resource's rows as events, with the
reader's access applied. `at` is the timestamp; `kind` is fixed or `{ field }`.
`refs` names reference columns whose labels reach `title` and `meta`.

```ts
timeline({
  kinds: Bot,
  sources: [
    timeline.source("telegram_message_log", { kind: { field: "kind" }, at: "createdAt", title: (m) => m.text }),
    timeline.source("notification_log", {
      kind: "failed",
      at: "createdAt",
      tone: "err",
      where: { failedReason: "__notnull__", deliveredAt: "__null__" },
      title: "Delivery failed",
    }),
  ],
});
```

On a record page a source reads only rows referencing the record, AND-ed with
`where`; `by` picks the column when several reference it. On a dashboard it reads
rows whose `at` is in the picked range.

`TimelineSource`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | `ResourceName` |  |
| `kind` | `string \| { field: keyof R & string }` | A fixed kind, or the field that holds each row's kind. With a field the chips narrow the read to the picked kinds, and a missing `title` prints the kind's label. |
| `at` | `keyof R & string` | The timestamp; a row without one is not an event. |
| `by?` | `keyof R & string` | The field that points at the viewed record when several do; mirrors `DetailTab.by`. |
| `where?` | `Where<R> \| ((ctx: WidgetContext) => Where<R>)` | Narrows the rows. On a record page the filter to the viewed record is always AND-ed in and `where` cannot set its field; on a dashboard the source reads the picked range. |
| `title?` | `\| string \| ((row: R, refs: Readonly<Record<string, string \| null>>, ctx: WidgetContext) => string)` | The line's title. Default: the kind's label. |
| `meta?` | `( row: R, refs: Readonly<Record<string, string \| null>>, ctx: WidgetContext, ) => string \| null \| undefined` | Trailing detail. |
| `body?` | `(row: R, ctx: WidgetContext) => string \| null \| undefined` | Longer text, folded under the line. |
| `tone?` | `Tone \| ((row: R) => Tone \| undefined)` | The dot's color. Default: the kind's tone. |
| `refs?` | `(keyof R & string)[]` | Reference columns whose labels `title` and `meta` read, resolved in one read per page. |
| `href?` | `false \| ((row: R, ctx: WidgetContext) => LinkTarget \| null)` | Default: the first `refs` record, else the row as its list opens it. `false`: no link. |
| `fold?` | `string` | One fold key for every event of the source. |
| `fields?` | `(keyof R & string)[]` | More fields the callbacks read, beyond the list's columns. |

#### TimelineEvent

`TimelineEvent`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | `Date` |  |
| `kind` | `string` | A key of the timeline's `kinds`. |
| `title` | `string` |  |
| `meta?` | `string` | Trailing detail — an amount, an owner, a platform. |
| `body?` | `string` | Longer text, folded under the line. |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | The dot's color. Default: the kind's tone. |
| `href?` | `LinkTarget` | Links the title — a path or a named target. |
| `fold?` | `string` | Consecutive events of one day and one kind with the same `fold` become one line. Default: the title. |
| `key?` | `string` | A stable identity for the line. |

#### TimelinePage

`TimelinePage`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `before` | `Date \| null` | Events at or before this moment; `null` for the newest page. |
| `limit` | `number` | Events to return at most: the page size, the ties already shown, and one more. |
| `kinds` | `readonly string[] \| null` | The kinds the reader picked; `null` for every kind. |

### heatmap

Activity per day over the last `days` days (91 by default) ending today, shaded in
four steps.

`source` counts rows, or sums `value`, per day of `at`. On a record page it reads
rows referencing the record, like a timeline source. It reads at most 10,000 rows;
beyond that use `query`, which returns totals per day.

```ts
heatmap({ label: "Visits, 13 weeks", source: { resource: "user_visit", at: "startedAt" }, unit: Visits });
```

The date picker does not move it.

`HeatmapOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `source?` | `HeatmapSource<N>` | Rows of a resource over the last `days` days, at most 10,000; past that, use `query`. |
| `query?` | `(ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<Array<{ at: Date \| string; value: number }>>` | Totals per day instead of `source`: `at` is a `Date` or a `YYYY-MM-DD` day. |
| `days?` | `number` | Days shown, ending today, from 7 to 371. Default: `91`. |
| `unit?` | `string \| PluralLabel` | What a day's value counts, for the summary and each day's tooltip. |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | The fill of a busy day. Default: `"accent"`. |
| `href?` | `(day: { from: Date; to: Date }, ctx: WidgetContext) => LinkTarget \| null` | Makes each day a link; `from` and `to` bound the day in the admin's zone. |
| `emptyState?` | `ReactNode` | Shown instead of the grid when every day is empty. Text or any node. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these channels fire. |

#### HeatmapSource

`HeatmapSource`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | `N` |  |
| `at` | `keyof RowOf<N> & string` | A timestamp, bucketed in the admin's zone, or a `YYYY-MM-DD` day. |
| `value?` | `keyof RowOf<N> & string` | Sum this field instead of counting rows. |
| `by?` | `keyof RowOf<N> & string` | The field that points at the viewed record when several do; mirrors `DetailTab.by`. |
| `where?` | `Where<RowOf<N>> \| ((ctx: WidgetContext) => Where<RowOf<N>>)` | Narrows the rows. On a record page the filter to the viewed record is always AND-ed in. |

### checklist

Items done or not. An item is done when `done` holds a value other than `null`,
`undefined`, `false`, a blank string or an empty list. The summary counts
non-`optional` items.

With `ordered`, done items show their date and the gap since the previous step.
`layout: "steps"` lays them out in a row. Not available in drawers.

```ts
checklist({
  label: "Journey",
  ordered: true,
  layout: "steps",
  items: async (c) => {
    const user = c.rowOf("user");
    return [
      { label: "Signed up", done: user.createdAt },
      { label: "Linked Telegram", done: user.telegramLinkedAt, optional: true },
      { label: "First reply sent", done: user.firstSentAt },
    ];
  },
});
```

`labels.checklist` words the summary, the gap and the marks' names for screen readers.

`ChecklistOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Card heading. |
| `items` | `ChecklistItem[] \| ((ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<ChecklistItem[]>)` | The items, or a function that reads them per request. |
| `ordered?` | `boolean` | Each done step shows when, and the time since the previous done step. |
| `layout?` | `"list" \| "steps"` | `"steps"` lays the items out in a row from the `md` breakpoint. Default: `"list"`. |
| `summary?` | `boolean` | "7 of 12" with a bar; optional items are not counted. Default: `true`. |
| `emptyState?` | `ReactNode` | Shown instead of the items when there are none. Text or any node. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run when any of these channels fire. |

#### ChecklistItem

`ChecklistItem`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `done` | `unknown` | Done unless `null`, `undefined`, `false`, a blank string or an empty list; `0` counts. A `Date` or an ISO string also says when, shown by an `ordered` checklist. |
| `hint?` | `string` | A muted note under the label. |
| `optional?` | `boolean` | Not counted in the summary; muted while not done. |
| `tone?` | `Tone` | The mark's color when done. Default: `"ok"`. |
| `href?` | `LinkTarget` | Links the label — a path or a named target. |
| `precision?` | `"day"` | The date has no clock: print the day, and measure no gap to or from it. A bare `YYYY-MM-DD` needs no flag. |

#### filled

One checklist item per labelled field, done when the field has a value.

```ts
checklist({
  label: "Profile",
  items: async (c) => filled(await profileOf(c), { bio: "About", hourlyRate: "Rate" }),
});
```

### custom

Your own component in the grid. `props` is a value or a server function. See
[Build a custom widget](/docs/customization/custom-widgets).

`CustomOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |
| `frame?` | `boolean` | Wrap the component in the standard widget card. Default: `true`. |
| `label?` | `string` | The card's title when framed, and the name errors and slow-widget timings use. |
| `minHeight?` | `number` | The height in px the widget keeps, while it loads and after, so the page below it does not jump when it arrives. |

### Charts

The chart builders come from `@flowpanel/kit`. Recharts loads only when a chart is on the page.

```ts
import { areaChart, barChart, lineChart, pieChart } from "@flowpanel/kit";
```

Each takes `(label, query, options)`. `x` and `y` (`category` and `value` on a pie)
are checked against the query's row type.

#### ChartOptionsBase

Shared by area, bar and line charts.

`ChartOptionsBase`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | `RowKey<R>` | Row key plotted on the x-axis. |
| `y?` | `RowKey<R> \| RowKey<R>[]` | Row key(s) plotted on the y-axis; an array draws one series per key. Default: every key of the first row except `x`, in its order — the columns a `series({ by })` returns. |
| `labels?` | `KeyLabels` | Legend and tooltip name per series key: a map, an `enumOf()` or a function. Default: the key. |
| `colors?` | `Readonly<Record<string, string>>` | A CSS colour per series key, e.g. `{ paid: "hsl(var(--fp-chart-1))" }`. Default: `--fp-data` for a single series, `--fp-chart-1…7` in `y` order for several. |
| `height?` | `number` | Chart height in px. Unset, it is 2/7 of the card's width, between 240 and 320. |
| `format?` | `NumericFormat` | How y-values are rendered in ticks and tooltips. |
| `minorUnits?` | `number` | The y-values are minor units with this many digits, as on a `money` field: with `format: "currency"`, `2` shows `260000` as $2,600. |
| `tooltip?` | `"default" \| "compact" \| false` | `false` omits the `<Tooltip>` entirely. |
| `drilldown?` | `Link` | Turns the whole card into a link — a path, a named target, or one computed from the context. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |
| `bucket?` | `ChartBucket` | How x-axis ticks print a date key. It does not aggregate: fold rows with `series({ grain })`. |

`ChartBucket` is `"minute" | "hour" | "day" | "week" | "month" | "year" | "auto"`.

Without `y`, the chart plots every numeric key of its first row except `x`, which
is what `series({ by })` returns. `labels` names the series. `bucket` only formats
date ticks; aggregate with `series({ grain })`. For amounts stored in cents, set
`format: "currency"` and `minorUnits: 2`, and the axis and tooltips show money.

One series draws in `--fp-data`; several use `--fp-chart-1` to `--fp-chart-7` in `y`
order. `colors` pins a series to a colour:

```ts
lineChart("Signups", signupsByPlan, {
  x: "day",
  y: ["trial", "paid"],
  colors: { paid: "hsl(var(--fp-chart-1))", trial: "hsl(var(--fp-chart-2))" },
});
```

#### areaChart

`AreaChartOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stacked?` | `boolean` | Stack multiple series instead of overlaying them. |
| `smooth?` | `boolean` | Draw curved rather than straight segments. |

#### barChart

`BarChartOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stacked?` | `boolean` | Stack multiple series instead of grouping them side by side. |
| `horizontal?` | `boolean` | Lay bars out horizontally. |

#### lineChart

`LineChartOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `smooth?` | `boolean` | Draw curved rather than straight segments. |
| `markers?` | `boolean` | Show a dot at every data point. |

#### pieChart

Pie charts take `category` / `value` instead of `x` / `y`. The slice legend is on
unless you pass `showLegend: false`.

`PieChartOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | `RowKey<R>` | Row key naming each slice. |
| `value` | `RowKey<R>` | Row key holding each slice's magnitude. |
| `donut?` | `boolean` | Cut a hole in the middle. |
| `showLegend?` | `boolean` | Show the slice legend. Default: `true`. |
| `height?` | `number` | Chart height in px. Unset, it is 2/7 of the card's width, between 240 and 320. |
| `span?` | `Span` | Width in the dashboard's 12-column grid. |
| `maxRange?` | `RangeLimit` | Cap the date range at its last N days — `"30d"` — for data kept only that long. |
| `drilldown?` | `Link` | Turns the whole card into a link — a path, a named target, or one computed from the context. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |
| `colors?` | `Record<string, string>` | Pin specific slices to a color, keyed by category value. |
| `format?` | `NumericFormat` | How slice values are rendered in the tooltip. |
| `tooltip?` | `"default" \| "compact" \| false` | `false` omits the `<Tooltip>` entirely. |

### Series helpers

Pure helpers that turn query rows into chart and bar data in the admin's zone.

One point per bucket across the range: hours, days, ISO weeks starting on Monday, or
months, bucketed in `range.timeZone`. Pass `ctx.dateRange` and the admin's zone
applies. Keys are `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00` for hours, which chart ticks
already read. `grain: "auto"` picks hours up to 2 days, days up to 92, weeks up to
400 and months beyond.

- **Gaps.** Every bucket is present. A bucket with no rows is `0` for a count or a
  sum, and whatever the `value` function returns for `[]`: return `null` for a ratio
  with no data.
- **Pivots.** Without `by` the one column is `value`, so a sparkline is
  `series(…).map((p) => p.value)`. With `by`, each value of that field is a column;
  `keys` fixes columns that must appear, in order. `top` keeps `keys` and the largest
  other series and folds the rest into `OTHER_KEY`, which charts name
  `labels.widget.other`.
- **Values.** `"12"` strings, bigints and booleans read as numbers. A `YYYY-MM-DD`
  value is that calendar day, and a zoneless timestamp such as `2026-09-21 09:00:00`
  is UTC, as everywhere else in FlowPanel.
- **Whole history.** A range starting at the epoch, such as a record page's
  `ctx.dateRange` without `detail.dateRange`, starts at the first row's bucket; with no
  rows there are no buckets.
- **DST.** On the day clocks skip an hour, that hour has no bucket. On the day they
  repeat one, both of its hours share one bucket.

Folding runs in JavaScript. Above about 50,000 rows, group by hour in SQL first.

`SeriesOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | `keyof R & string` | The timestamp or `YYYY-MM-DD` field that places a row in a bucket. |
| `value?` | `Fold<R>` | How a bucket's rows become its number. Default: the row count. |
| `by?` | `keyof R & string` | One column per value of this field; without it the one column is `value`. |
| `keys?` | `readonly string[]` | Values of `by` present as columns, in this order, even with no rows. |
| `grain?` | `Grain` | `"auto"`: hours up to 2 days, days up to 92, weeks up to 400, else months. Weeks start Monday. Default: `"auto"`. |
| `top?` | `number` | Keep `keys` and the N largest other series; the rest fold into `OTHER_KEY`. |

One ranked `BarRow` per value of `by`, with `key` and `share`, and each row's
`previous` when you pass the earlier period's rows as `previous`. `top` folds
the rest into one `OTHER_KEY` row, so the shares still add up to 1. `labels` takes a
map, an `enumOf()` or a function. Shares only mean something for counts and sums.

`BreakdownOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `by` | `keyof R & string` | One row per value of this field. |
| `value?` | `Fold<R>` | How a value's rows become its number. Default: the row count. |
| `keys?` | `readonly string[]` | Values always present, at zero when no row has them. |
| `labels?` | `KeyLabels` | Row labels: a map, an `enumOf()`, or a function. Default: the value itself. |
| `top?` | `number` | Keep `keys` and the N largest other rows; the rest fold into one `OTHER_KEY` row. |
| `previous?` | `readonly R[]` | The compared period's rows, folded the same way into each row's `previous`. |
| `href?` | `(key: string) => LinkTarget \| null` | Where a row's label leads. |

A preset's bounds now, in the admin's zone, for a query that needs a fixed window
beside the picked one. Pass the same `now` to widgets sharing a query.

```ts
import { barChart, bars, breakdown, series, type WidgetContext } from "@flowpanel/kit";

const hourly = (c: WidgetContext) => c.sql<{ at: Date; platform: string; orders: number }>`
  select hour as at, platform, orders_new as orders
  from scraper_hourly_stats where hour >= ${c.dateRange.from} and hour < ${c.dateRange.to}`;

bars({
  label: "New orders by marketplace",
  share: true,
  query: async (c) => breakdown(await c.query(hourly), { by: "platform", value: "orders", labels: Platform }),
});
barChart(
  "New orders by day",
  async (c) => series(await c.query(hourly), c.dateRange, { at: "at", by: "platform", value: "orders", grain: "day" }),
  { x: "date", labels: Platform, stacked: true },
);
```

The range of the same length ending where the given one begins, in elapsed time.
`ctx.dateRange.previous` is usually what you want.

Equals `series(rows, dateRange, { at: dateField, value: valueField, grain: "day" })`.

### Dashboards

Both return their argument, typed.

`DashboardConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | Path under `paths.admin`. `"/"` makes this the admin's landing page. |
| `label` | `string` | Nav entry and page title. |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered in navigation and the command palette. |
| `navGroup?` | `NavGroupRef` | Sidebar group for this entry. Default: the kind's own group — Dashboards or Pages. |
| `dateRange?` | `DateRangeConfig` | Adds a date picker whose value reaches every widget query. |
| `filters?` | `DashboardFilter[]` | Selects beside the date picker; the values reach every widget as `ctx.filters`. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeOption` | Re-run the query when any of these fire: a channel name, or `{ resource }` for that resource's own changes. |
| `refresh?` | ``${number}s` \| `${number}m`` | Re-renders the whole dashboard on an interval, e.g. `"60s"` or `"5m"`; paused while the tab is hidden. |
| `sections` | `SectionConfig[]` | Widget bands, rendered top to bottom. |
| `actions?` | `DashboardAction<any, any>[]` | Optional top-bar action buttons rendered in the dashboard page header. |
| `hideActionsBar?` | `boolean` | Hide the default `DashboardActionsBar`. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Who may see and open this dashboard and run its actions. |

`refresh` (`"<n>s"` or `"<n>m"`) re-renders the dashboard on that interval while the
tab is visible and shows the data's age by the date picker.

#### SectionConfig

`SectionConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | Section heading. Omit for an untitled band. |
| `description?` | `string` | Supporting copy under the heading. |
| `columns?` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 6 \| 12` | Grid columns the widgets lay out across; omitted, 12 when a widget sets `span`. Default: `1`. |
| `variant?` | `"cards" \| "strip"` | `"strip"` draws the section's `metric`/`stat` widgets as one band with no card; another kind warns in development. Default: `"cards"`. |
| `align?` | `"stretch" \| "start"` | How cards in one row size: `"stretch"` to the tallest, `"start"` each to its content. Default: a `table` or `list` keeps its own height, every other card stretches. |
| `widgets` | `WidgetConfig[]` |  |

`variant: "strip"` draws `metric` and `stat` widgets as one band without cards.
`columns` sets cells per line (up to six by default; two on a phone). A record
page's [`detail.stats`](/docs/reference/resources#record-page) is the same strip.

In a `"cards"` section, `table` and `list` cards keep their height and others
stretch to the row; `align: "start"` or `"stretch"` sets it for all.

```ts
{ variant: "strip", widgets: [newOrders, runs, successRate, bans] }
```

#### DateRangeConfig

`DateRangeConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `preset?` | `DateRangePreset` | Range selected on first load; one outside `presets` is dropped with a development warning. |
| `default?` | `{ from: Date; to: Date }` | Explicit range used when no preset is given. |
| `presets?` | `DateRangePreset[]` | Presets the picker offers, in order. A URL preset outside the list is ignored, and without `preset` or `default` the first entry is selected. Default: all seven. |

`DateRangePreset` is `"today" | "yesterday" | "last7d" | "last30d" | "last12m" | "MTD" | "QTD" | "YTD"`.

`today`, `yesterday`, `MTD`, `QTD` and `YTD` start at midnight in `formatting.timeZone`
(UTC when it is not set); `last7d` and `last30d` are the last 7 × 24 and 30 × 24 hours.
`last12m` starts on the 1st of the month eleven months back, so a monthly chart gets
twelve buckets, the current month included; it compares with the same range a year back.

`presets` limits the picker's choices; `preset` defaults to the first.

#### DashboardFilter

`DashboardFilter`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | The URL key `f_<key>`, as a list's filters use, and the key in `ctx.filters`. |
| `label` | `string` | The select's label. |
| `options` | `SelectOption[] \| EnumDef \| ((ctx: WidgetContext) => Promise<SelectOption[]>)` | The choices: a list, an `enumOf()`, or a function of the context. |

`filters` adds a select per entry beside the date picker, stored in the URL as
`f_<key>`. `options` takes `SelectOption[]`, an `enumOf()`, or a function of the
widget context; a plain string list is not accepted.

`filterOnClick: "<key>"` on `bars`, `tracker` or `table` sets that filter on click,
replacing the row's link. It is rejected on a record page or in a drawer.

```ts
const byPlatform: DashboardFilter = { key: "platform", label: "Marketplace", options: Platform };

const hourly = (c: WidgetContext) => c.sql<HourRow>`
  select hour as at, platform, runs_total as runs from scraper_hourly_stats
  where hour >= ${c.dateRange.from} and hour < ${c.dateRange.to}
    and (${c.filters.platform ?? null}::text is null or platform = ${c.filters.platform ?? null})`;

dashboard({
  path: "/parsing",
  label: "Parsing",
  filters: [byPlatform],
  sections: [{ columns: 12, widgets: [tracker({ query: hourly, at: "at", by: "platform", filterOnClick: "platform", span: 12 })] }],
});
```

#### ResolvedDateRange

`ResolvedDateRange`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `Date` |  |
| `to` | `Date` |  |
| `preset` | `DateRangePreset \| "custom"` | `"custom"` once the operator picks their own dates. |

#### WidgetDateRange

`WidgetDateRange`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `previous` | `{ from: Date; to: Date } \| null` | The period compared against: the same stretch a day, month, quarter or year back for a calendar preset, else the span before it. `null` when there is no earlier period to query. |
| `timeZone` | `string` | IANA zone the admin renders and buckets in — `formatting.timeZone`, else `"UTC"`. |

#### PageConfig

`PageConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | Path under `paths.admin`. |
| `label` | `string` | Nav entry and page title. |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered in navigation and the command palette. |
| `navGroup?` | `NavGroupRef` | Sidebar group for this entry. Default: the kind's own group — Dashboards or Pages. |
