| `component?` | `ComponentType<Record<string, never>>` | Server or client React component rendered at `<paths.admin><path>`. |
| `href?` | `string` | External href used when `component` is not provided. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Who may see and open this page. |

## queue()

The queue builder, its options, and how a queue key becomes a route.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/queues

Documented types: queue, QueueOptions, QueueConfig

`queue(ref, options)` registers a BullMQ queue as a navigation entry whose page
embeds [bull-board](https://github.com/felixmosh/bull-board). Setup and security:
[Queues](/docs/guides/queues).

```ts
import { defineAdmin, queue } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import { emailQueue } from "@/lib/queues";

export default defineAdmin({
  adapter,
  auth: flowpanelAuth,
  queues: [
    queue(emailQueue, {
      label: "Email",
      boardUrl: "http://localhost:3001/queue/email",
      boardSecret: process.env.BOARD_SECRET,
      access: "admin",
    }),
  ],
});
```

`ref` is typed `unknown`; FlowPanel reads only its `.name`, when `options.key` is
absent.

With `boardSecret`, each render of the queue page adds
`?fp_board=link.<key>.<expires>.<signature>` to `boardUrl`: an HMAC-SHA256 of the
queue key and an expiry one minute ahead, keyed by the secret. `startBoardServer`
with the same `auth.secret` checks the signature, the expiry and that the key names
one of its queues, then adds that queue to a signed session cookie. Each queue in
the session expires an hour after its own latest link, so opening one queue page
never keeps another alive. The board shows, and acts on, only the queues in the
session, so a user who may open one queue page cannot reach another queue on the
same board; Redis-wide statistics and the metrics of other queues answer `404` to
a session. The
secret never reaches the browser. A copied link works for its minute, for its one
queue. The queue key must be the BullMQ queue's name or its key in the board's
`queues`. `boardUrl` may be relative when the board sits behind the admin's own
proxy.

### startBoardServer

`startBoardServer(options)` from `@flowpanel/kit/bullmq/board` starts the board on
its own port and returns the Node `Server`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queues` | required | The BullMQ queues to show, keyed by name |
| `auth.secret` | required | Checks signed links; also accepted as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` from a reverse proxy, which reaches every queue. A list accepts each secret and signs sessions with the first, so a secret can rotate |
| `port` | `3001` | Port to listen on |
| `bindHost` | `127.0.0.1` | Interface to bind |
| `basePath` | `/` | Path the board is mounted at, and the cookie's path |
| `trustedProxies` | `0` | Proxies in front that set `X-Forwarded-Proto`; with one, the session cookie is `Secure` behind TLS termination |

A request without a valid link, cookie or bearer gets `401`. `auth.token` and
`?token=` links are gone: `startBoardServer` throws when given `auth.token`.

### QueueOptions

`QueueOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | Nav entry and page title for this queue. |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered in navigation and the command palette. |
| `hidden?` | `boolean` | Keep the queue route registered but omit it from primary navigation. |
| `navGroup?` | `NavGroupRef` | Sidebar group for this queue. Default: the Queues group. |
| `boardUrl` | `string` | Full URL (e.g., http://localhost:3001/queue/email) to the bull-board UI. |
| `boardSecret?` | `string` | The board server's `auth.secret`. The page then adds a link signed for this queue that expires in a minute, so the secret itself never reaches the browser. |
| `key?` | `string` | Optional explicit key; defaults to queue.name. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Who may see and open this queue page. |

`access` takes the same `AccessRule` as a resource: a role, a list of roles, or a function.

### QueueConfig

What `queue()` returns.

`QueueConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `__kind` | `"queue"` |  |
| `ref` | `QueueRef` |  |
| `options` | `QueueOptions` |  |

### The key, and the URL it produces

`key` defaults to `ref.name`, and the page is `<paths.admin>/queues/<key>`, such as
`/admin/queues/email`. `defineAdmin` rejects a queue when:

| Condition | Error |
| --- | --- |
| No `.name` on the ref **and** no `options.key` | `[flowpanel] queues[<index>]: the queue has no name to key it by. Set key in its options.` |
| Two queues resolve to the same key | `[flowpanel] queue "<key>": two queues use this key. Give each queue its own key.` |
| The key is `dashboards`, `drawer`, `export` or `queues` | `[flowpanel] queue "<key>": the name is one FlowPanel's routing reserves…` |

### Reading queue state from your own code

To count jobs in a widget, wrap the same `Queue` instances with `bullmqAdapter`:

```ts
import { bullmqAdapter } from "@flowpanel/kit/bullmq";
import { emailQueue, scrapeQueue } from "@/lib/queues";

export const jobs = bullmqAdapter({ email: emailQueue, scrape: scrapeQueue });
```

```ts
import { metric } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import { jobs } from "@/lib/queue-adapter";

metric("Failed jobs", async () => jobs.queues.email.getJobCountByTypes("failed"), {
  tone: "err",
  drilldown: "/admin/queues/email",
});
```

A queue page has no named link target, so the link spells the path.
`BullMQAdapter` is `{ kind: "bullmq"; queues: Record<string, Queue> }`.

### Peer dependencies

All optional; install them only for queues:

```bash
pnpm add bullmq ioredis
pnpm add @bull-board/api @bull-board/express express
```

## Contexts

What your queries, mutations and actions receive at runtime.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/contexts

Documented types: RequestContext, QueryContext, ListQueryContext, ItemQueryContext, MutationContext, ActionContext, FilterRangeValue, FilterInValue

Adapter methods, mutations, actions and option resolvers receive a context that
extends `RequestContext`, so `session`, `role` and `scope` are there. Widgets and
record pages get their own: `WidgetContext` has `session` but no `role` or `scope`,
`DetailTabContext` is a subset of `WidgetContext`, and `DetailHeaderContext` has
only `format`, `labels` and `link`.

### RequestContext

`RequestContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requestId?` | `string` | Stable correlation id generated once per request. |
| `req` | `Request` | The incoming request. Built from the real headers, even during page renders. |
| `session` | `Session \| null` | Result of `AuthConfig.session` for this request. |
| `role` | `string` | Result of `AuthConfig.role` for this session. |
| `scope` | `Scope` | Tenant scope resolved by the admin-wide `scope`. Null when unscoped. |
| `ip` | `string \| null` | Caller IP as the proxies counted in `security.trustedProxies` recorded it, else `null`. For logs and rate limits, not for authentication. |
| `userAgent` | `string \| null` |  |

`req` carries the incoming headers during server renders too.

### QueryContext

Base context for reads. Field `options` and `defaultValue` resolvers receive it. Widget queries receive [`WidgetContext`](/docs/reference/widgets#widgetcontext) instead.

`QueryContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unsafe?` | `{ db: Db }` | Explicit escape hatch for trusted application callbacks. |
| `dateRange` | `{ from: Date; to: Date }` | Active date range — the dashboard picker, or all-time elsewhere. |
| `searchParams` | `URLSearchParams` | Query string of the page being rendered. |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal` | Aborted when the request is cancelled. Pass it to long queries. |
| `select?` | `readonly string[]` | Explicit adapter projection. Omitted preserves the legacy full-row read; `[]` returns no values. Adapters must not substitute a primary key or full row for an empty selection. |
| `boundScope?` | `BoundAdapterScope` | Opaque request-bound tenant policy. |

### ListQueryContext

What an adapter's `list` receives: everything needed to build one page of rows.

`ListQueryContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filters` | `Record<string, unknown>` | Filter values keyed by declared field name. |
| `sort` | `{ field: keyof Row & string; dir: "asc" \| "desc" } \| null` | Active sort, or null when the list is unsorted. |
| `tiebreak?` | `readonly string[]` | Columns ordered by after `sort`, ascending, so pages never overlap: the primary key's. |
| `page` | `number` | 1-based page number. |
| `pageSize` | `number` |  |
| `search` | `string` | Current search term. Empty string when the box is blank. |
| `searchFields?` | `string[]` | Allowlist of columns `search` is OR-ed across, taken verbatim from `resource.options.search`. |
| `softDelete?` | `{ column: string }` | Set when the resource declares `delete.softDelete` — deleted rows are filtered out. |
| `includeDeleted?` | `boolean` | Include soft-deleted rows, for the "show deleted" view. |

`searchFields` is `options.search`. An adapter must search only these columns.

### ItemQueryContext

`ItemQueryContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Primary key of the requested row, as it appeared in the URL. |

### MutationContext

What an adapter's `create`, `update`, `delete` and `restore` receive.

`MutationContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `db` | `Db` | Your database client, exactly as handed to the adapter. |
| `input` | `Partial<Row>` | Values to write, already coerced and validated. |
| `id?` | `string` | Target row id. Absent on create. |
| `softDelete?` | `{ column: string }` | Set when the resource declares `delete.softDelete` — delete stamps the column. |
| `boundScope?` | `BoundAdapterScope` | Opaque request-bound tenant policy. |

### ActionContext

What every action's `run` receives.

`ActionContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unsafe?` | `{ db: Db }` | Explicit escape hatch for trusted action implementations. |
| `actorId` | `string \| null` | Caller identity — same derivation the audit trail uses (`auth.userId`, then `session.id`, then `session.user.id`). |
| `publish` | `(channel: string, payload?: unknown) => Promise<void>` | Push a realtime message to every connected admin. |

### Filter values

Most filters arrive in `ctx.filters` as scalars. Two arrive structured, with
type guards.

#### FilterRangeValue

Produced by `daterange` and `numeric-range` filters.

A `daterange` day such as `2026-09-23` covers that whole day in
`formatting.timeZone` (UTC if unset). A widget link writes ISO instants joined by
`~`, which arrive unchanged.

`FilterRangeValue`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `op` | `"range"` |  |
| `gte?` | `number \| Date` |  |
| `lte?` | `number \| Date` |  |

#### FilterInValue

Produced by `multiselect` filters: match any of `values`.

`FilterInValue`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `op` | `"in"` |  |
| `values` | `string[]` |  |

#### Narrowing them

```ts
import { isFilterInValue, isFilterRangeValue, type ListQueryContext } from "@flowpanel/kit";

export function readFilters(ctx: ListQueryContext<Record<string, unknown>>): void {
  for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(ctx.filters)) {
    if (isFilterRangeValue(value)) {
      console.log(field, value.gte, value.lte);
    } else if (isFilterInValue(value)) {
      console.log(field, value.values);
    } else {
      console.log(field, value);
    }
  }
}
```

### Raw SQL and counts

A [`WidgetContext`](/docs/reference/widgets#widgetcontext) and a
`DetailTabContext` carry `ctx.sql`, `ctx.count`, `ctx.read` and `ctx.rowOf`.

#### ctx.sql

`ctx.sql` runs the statement as written, with no tenant scope, access rule or
soft-delete filter. Add those predicates yourself, or use `ctx.count` and
`ctx.read`, which apply them.

```ts
metric("New signups", async (ctx) => {
  const [row] = await ctx.sql<{ n: number }>`
    select count(*)::int as n
    from users
    where created_at >= ${ctx.dateRange.from}
  `;
  return row?.n ?? 0;
});
```

Every interpolated value is a bound parameter. A `Date` binds as ISO-8601 text and
a `bigint` as decimal text. Arrays bind differently per adapter; see
[Raw SQL](/docs/reference/adapters#raw-sql). Drizzle `sql` fragments nest:

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { stat, type WidgetContext } from "@flowpanel/kit";

const window = (c: WidgetContext) => sql`hour >= ${c.dateRange.from} and hour < ${c.dateRange.to}`;

stat("Runs in the period", async (ctx) => {
  const rows = await ctx.sql<HourRow>`select * from scraper_hourly_stats where ${window(ctx)}`;
  return rows.reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.runs, 0);
});
```

Cast counts and sums in SQL (`count(*)::int`, `sum(x)::float8`): Postgres returns
`int8` and `numeric` as strings.

A string shaped like a zoneless `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` comes back as a UTC `Date`.
`parseDates: false` on the adapter turns that off. `ctx.sql` throws when the
adapter has no `sql` capability.

#### ctx.count

`ctx.count(resource, where, { range })` counts rows with the resource's access,
scope and soft-delete rules; a resource or field the session may not read counts
`0`. `where` takes [where values](#where-values). An `undefined`, `null` or `""`
value counts `0` and warns in development. A misspelt field throws.

```ts
stat("Open tickets", (ctx) => ctx.count("tickets", { status: "open" }));
```

#### Counting and reading a period

`range` names the timestamp field bounded by `ctx.dateRange`, inclusive. Over a
whole history it adds no bound.

```ts
metric("Visits", (ctx) => ctx.count("user_visit", { userId: ctx.id }, { range: "startedAt" }), {
  compare: true,
});
```

A `{ gte, lte }` on the same field in `where` narrows to the overlap.

#### ctx.read

`ctx.read(resource, options)` returns rows with the same rules as the resource's
list; an unreadable resource returns `[]`. Identical reads share one query per
request.

```ts
const profileOf = async (ctx: WidgetContext) =>
  (
    await ctx.read("freelancer_profile", {
      where: { userId: ctx.id },
      fields: ["hourlyRate"],
      limit: 1,
    })
  )[0] ?? null;

kv({ label: "Profile", items: [{ label: "Rate", value: async (c) => (await profileOf(c))?.hourlyRate }] });
```

Rows carry the list's columns, `expose` and `rowKey`, plus `fields`; other
properties are `undefined`. `limit` defaults to 100, maximum 1000. A misspelt name
throws before any query.

#### ctx.rowOf

`ctx.rowOf(resource)` is the viewed record, typed. It throws on a dashboard or on
another resource's page. `ctx.row` is the untyped record.

```ts
stat("With us", async (c) => c.format.relative(c.rowOf("user").createdAt));
```

#### Where values

A `where` is keyed by the row's fields. Each value is one of:

| Value | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `"paid"`, `42`, `true`, a `Date` | rows equal to it |
| `"__null__"` / `"__notnull__"` | rows where the field is empty / not empty |
| `{ gte, lte }` (numbers or dates, either side optional) | rows inside the bounds, inclusive |
| `["paid", "refunded"]`, `[1, 2]` | rows equal to any of them; an empty array matches nothing; pass a boolean as a plain value, not in an array |
| `{ op: "in", values }`, `{ op: "range", gte, lte }` | the adapter's own filter shapes |

`ctx.read` throws on `undefined`, `null`, `""`, an empty range, or an array holding
a boolean. Leave the field out, or pass `"__null__"`.

### Request-scoped access

Read the current context from AsyncLocalStorage when you cannot pass it down.

```ts
import { getRequestContext, tryGetRequestContext } from "@flowpanel/kit";

const ctx = getRequestContext();      // throws outside a request
const maybe = tryGetRequestContext(); // null outside a request
```

`runWithRequestContext(ctx, fn)` sets it; FlowPanel already wraps adapter calls
and action `run` in it.

## Type registry

FlowpanelTypes, FlowpanelResources, and the types that resolve through them.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/registry

FlowPanel takes your types from the database client, Drizzle schema and auth
instance you register once, with no code generator:

```ts
import type { auth } from "@/lib/auth";
import type { db } from "@/db";
import type * as schema from "@/db/schema";

declare module "@flowpanel/kit" {
  interface FlowpanelTypes {
    db: typeof db;
    schema: typeof schema;
    session: typeof auth.$Infer.Session;
  }
}
```

Augment the module you import from, `"@flowpanel/kit"` for a kit install. Put the
block in one file that TypeScript includes, such as `flowpanel.config.ts`. Every
entry is optional: without it the types fall back to `unknown`, `string` or
`Record<string, unknown>`, and `defineAdmin` still
[checks names at startup](/docs/build/resources#typos-and-column-validation).

### FlowpanelTypes

A registry for framework-wide type bindings: `db`, `schema` and `session`.

```ts
interface FlowpanelTypes {}
```

#### InferDB

```ts
type InferDB = FlowpanelTypes extends { db: infer D } ? D : unknown;
```

`InferDB` is the default `Db` parameter of:

| Declaration | Reached from |
| --- | --- |
| `WidgetContext<DB = InferDB>` | every widget `query`, a `StatItem.value` resolver, a `custom()` widget's `props` resolver |
| `ActionContext<Db = InferDB>` | every row, bulk, dashboard and drawer action `run`; those signatures name `ActionContext<InferDB>` explicitly |
| `Adapter<DB = InferDB, Ref = unknown>` | the adapter's own `db` property |

The adapter contexts (`QueryContext` and those built on it) default `Db` to
`unknown`, and carry no client: a `FieldDef.options` or `defaultValue` resolver
queries through your own `db` import.

#### schema

Register the Drizzle schema and every table and view becomes a resource name with
its row, keyed by SQL name: `pgTable("user_visit", …)` is `"user_visit"`.
`ResourceName`, `RowOf`, `InferRow` and `ReferenceSpec` read it, so a misspelt name
in `ctx.count`, `ctx.read` or a `reference` fails to compile.

#### session

Register the session type (`typeof auth.$Infer.Session` for better-auth) and
`Session` is that type in `ctx.session`, `auth` callbacks, `theme` and scope
callbacks. Otherwise it is `Record<string, unknown>`.

#### RowOf

```ts
type RowOf<N extends string> = N extends keyof AllResources ? AllResources[N] : Record<string, unknown>;
```

The row of a known resource.

### FlowpanelResources

A map of resource name to row type, keyed by the name `defineAdmin` uses (the SQL
table name unless `options.name` is set). With Prisma, register every model here,
under the resource's `name` when it has one, as `flowpanel new` does:

```ts
declare module "@flowpanel/kit" {
  interface FlowpanelResources {
    users: import("@prisma/client").User;
  }
}
```

With a registered Drizzle `schema`, add an entry only for a renamed resource, such
as `user: typeof schema.adminUserRow.$inferSelect`. An entry replaces the schema's
row of the same name.

```ts
interface FlowpanelResources {}
```

#### InferRow

```ts
type InferRow<Ref> = Ref extends { $inferSelect: infer R }
  ? R
  : Ref extends keyof AllResources
    ? AllResources[Ref]
    : Record<string, unknown>;
```

`resource(ref, options)` types `options` by `InferRow<Ref>`: a Drizzle table's
`$inferSelect`, a registered name's row, or `Record<string, unknown>`. With
`options.name`, a string ref such as a Prisma model reads the row registered under
that name first, so `resource("User", { name: "users" })` checks its columns against
the `users` entry.

#### ResourceName

```ts
type ResourceName = [keyof AllResources] extends [never]
  ? string
  : keyof AllResources & string;
```

The type of a resource name used elsewhere in config: a tab's `resource`, a
`table({ resource })`, `ctx.count`. Plain `string` while the registry is empty.

#### ReferenceSpec

```ts
type ReferenceSpec = [keyof AllResources] extends [never]
  ? { resource: string; labelField: string }
  : {
      [R in keyof AllResources]: {
        resource: R;
        labelField: keyof AllResources[R] & string;
      };
    }[keyof AllResources];
```

A foreign-key target for `ColumnDef.reference` and `FieldDef.reference`.
`labelField` must be a column of the named resource.

```ts
{ field: "userId", reference: { resource: "users", labelField: "email" } }
//                                                  ^ keyof users row, not of orders
```

## React components

The full @flowpanel/kit/react export surface, grouped by what it's for.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/react-components

Documented types: AdminShellProps, DrawerProps, CommandPaletteProps, DataTableProps, DataTableColumn, AutoFormProps, FormProps, FieldProps, FlowpanelIconProps, DevToolsPanelProps

The components the admin renders with, for custom slots, pages and `"bare"`-shell
chrome. Import them from `@flowpanel/kit/react`.

```ts
import { AutoForm, DataTable, useAdminTable } from "@flowpanel/kit/react";
```

Not listed here: `@flowpanel/kit/client` holds
[`useAdminMutation`](/docs/reference/client), and `@flowpanel/kit/charts` the
[chart components](/docs/customization/charts#client-data).

### Shell

| Export | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `AdminShell` | Visual chrome around admin content, in a sidebar or tab-strip variant. |
| `AdminNav` | Renders `NavGroup[]` as the sidebar nav; a `collapsible` group folds under its label until it holds the current page. |
| `AdminTabs` | Tab-strip variant of the nav, used when `AdminShellVariant` is `"tabs"`. |
| `AccountMenu` | User menu (avatar, name, sign-out) shown in the shell header. |
| `Brand` | Renders a `ShellBrand` (logo/name) in the shell header. |
| `Breadcrumbs` | Breadcrumb trail from a `BreadcrumbItem[]`. |
| `CommandPalette` | The ⌘K command palette, built on `cmdk`. |
| `Drawer`, `DrawerHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerFooter` | Side-variant drawer built on Radix Dialog, and its section slots. A `DrawerTitle` is the visible heading that names the dialog; without one, `title` (or `labels.drawer.title`) names it for screen readers. On close, focus goes back to the element that opened the drawer, or to `returnFocus()` when that element is gone. |
| `DetailShell` | Chrome around a resource detail page. |
| `FlowpanelGlobals` | Mounts the component, formatting, API-base and label providers, the realtime provider, the toast host and the theme runtime, once per admin. |
| `PageHeader`, `DefaultPageHeader` | Page title/description/actions header and its default renderer. `badges` renders several pills in order, each an optional link. |
| `ShortcutsCheatsheet` | The keyboard shortcuts sheet. `FlowpanelGlobals` mounts it: `?` opens it and `/` focuses the list's search box, outside text fields. Without `shortcuts` it lists the admin's own keys in its labels' language. |
| `ThemeScript` | Inline script that applies the stored theme class before hydration, avoiding a flash. |
| `ComponentsProvider`, `useComponents` | Provider/reader for the `FlowpanelComponentSlots` override map. |
| `useComponent` | Resolves a single slot: `useComponent("Pagination", DefaultPagination)` returns the host override when there is one, otherwise the default you passed. |
| `useComponentOverrides` | The raw override map from the nearest `ComponentsProvider`, without defaults filled in. |
| `LabelsProvider`, `useLabels` | Provider/reader for label overrides (pluralization, field labels). |
| `FormattingProvider`, `useFormatting` | Provider/reader for the resolved locale, time zone and currency. |
| `ApiBaseProvider`, `useApiBase` | Provider/reader for the API mount (`paths.api`, default `/api/flowpanel`), including a Next.js `basePath`. |

### Data table & filters

| Export | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `DataTable` | The resource list table: sorting, pagination, selection, inline edit, realtime refresh. |
| `BulkBar` | Floating action bar shown when `DataTable` rows are selected. |
| `ColumnPinMenu` | Per-column menu for pinning left/right. |
| `ColumnVisibilityMenu` | Toolbar menu for showing/hiding columns. |
| `DensityToggle` | Toggles `DataTableDensity` (row spacing) in the toolbar. |
| `FilterBar` | Renders a `FilterBarSpec[]` as the filter row above the table. |
| `FilterSheet` | Shows its children in line from the `sm` breakpoint up, and on a phone behind one "Filters (n)" button that opens them in a bottom sheet. `active` is the number of set filters. |
| `BooleanFilter`, `DateRangeFilter`, `MultiSelectFilter`, `NumericRangeFilter`, `SelectFilter`, `TagFilter`, `TextFilter` | One filter control per `ColumnMeta.type`, each driven by `FilterBar`. `DateRangeFilter` opens a two-month range calendar with presets. |
| `DateRangePicker` | Standalone preset dropdown (Today, Last 7 days, MTD, …) for dashboards; `presets` narrows and orders the list, and a `from`/`to` value without a preset shows as its two days. |
| `Pagination`, `DefaultPagination` | Page controls under the table and their default renderer. |
| `ArrayCell`, `JsonCell`, `ReferenceCell` | Read-only cell renderers for array, JSON, and reference columns. |
| `InlineEditCell` | Editable cell used when a column declares `editable: true`. |
| `JsonEditor` | Structured editor for a JSON column, used by `InlineEditCell` and forms. |
| `ReferencePicker` | Search-and-select control for picking a referenced row. |
| `MobileCardList` | Card layout `DataTable` switches to under the mobile breakpoint. |
| `KV`, `KVRow` | Key/value list layout, used by card and drawer field views. |
| `renderFormatCell` | Renders a declarative `ColumnFormat` value. `DataTable` cells call it internally. |
| `HeatCell`, `UrlCell`, `RelativeTimeCell`, `BooleanCell`, `ToneText` | The cells `renderFormatCell` renders for a heat percent, a url, a relative time, a boolean and a number coloured by its threshold. Use them in a custom cell to match the table. |

`DataTableProps`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `DataTableColumn<Row>[]` |  |
| `rows` | `Row[]` |  |
| `total` | `number` |  |

| `columnVisibility?` | `Record<string, boolean>` |  |
| `columnWidths?` | `Record<string, number>` |  |
| `onColumnWidthsChange?` | `(widths: Record<string, number>) => void` |  |
| `pinnedColumns?` | `{ left?: string[]; right?: string[] }` |  |
| `onPinnedColumnsChange?` | `(pinned: { left?: string[]; right?: string[] }) => void` |  |
| `realtime?` | `string \| { channel: string; debounceMs?: number }` | Subscribe to an SSE channel and trigger `router.refresh()` on events. |
| `rowEndCell?` | `(row: Row, rowIndex: number) => React.ReactNode` |  |
| `rowEndCellRem?` | `number` | The trailing column's width in rem; the default 3.5 holds the row menu. |
| `rowEndCellLabel?` | `string` | Accessible label for the trailing column header. Defaults to "Actions". |
| `onEditRow?` | `(row: Row) => void` | Triggered when the user presses `e` on a focused row. |
| `onDeleteRow?` | `(row: Row) => void` | Triggered when the user presses `d` on a focused row. |
| `onFocusSearch?` | `() => void` | Triggered when the user presses `/`. Typically focuses the search input. |
| `onShowShortcuts?` | `() => void` | Triggered when the user presses `?`. Typically opens the cheatsheet. |
| `inlineEditResource?` | `string` |  |
| `mobileLayout?` | `"card" \| "scroll" \| false` | Mobile layout when the viewport is narrower than 640px. |
| `enteringRowKeys?` | `string[]` | Stable keys that should receive the one-shot, reduced-motion-safe entry treatment. |
| `exportable?` | `boolean \| { formats?: ("csv" \| "json")[]; fields?: string[]; resource?: string }` | When set, renders an "Export" button in the toolbar. With `resource`, the server exports every row matching the page's filters; without it, the rows on screen are downloaded. |
| `importable?` | `{ resource: string; formats: ("csv" \| "json")[] }` |  |
| `showDensityToggle?` | `boolean` |  |
| `rowLabel?` | `string` | What one row is, mid-sentence ("run"): phone cards read "Open run 36". |

Each column of a `DataTable` you render yourself is a `DataTableColumn`. Its width follows its kind, `content` and `textRem`, measured against the table's own width, so give the table a width from its parent (`flex-1 min-w-0` in a flex row). Pass `textRem`, the widest value's width in rem, for content-sized columns: a text column then never narrows below its widest value or 13rem, whichever is less. Without it, a text column can narrow to between 7 and 10rem by its kind, or its header.

`DataTableColumn`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `keyof Row & string` |  |
| `label?` | `string` |  |
| `render?` | `(row: Row) => React.ReactNode` |  |
| `sortable?` | `boolean` |  |
| `width?` | `number \| string` | Fixed width: px as a number, or a `"px"` or `"rem"` string, so the other columns can fit around it. |
| `align?` | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"` |  |
| `hidden?` | `boolean` |  |
| `className?` | `string` |  |
| `type?` | `"string" \| "number" \| "boolean" \| "date" \| "json" \| "enum" \| "array" \| "reference"` | Adapter introspection hint propagated from `ColumnMeta.type`. |
| `editable?` | `boolean` |  |
| `format?` | `ColumnFormat` | Declarative formatter mirrored from `ColumnDef.format`. |
| `secondary?` | `keyof Row & string` | A field of the row shown as a muted second line under the cell. |
| `content?` | `"long" \| "email" \| "link"` | What a text column holds, which sizes it: long text and an email get more room, a link a little. Field names no longer decide it; set it yourself. |
| `textRem?` | `number` | Optional: the widest value in this column, in rem at the table's text size. Its ideal width fits it; without it the column takes its kind's default. |

### Forms

| Export | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `AutoForm` | Renders a resource's create/update fields from `ResolvedField[]` or `ColumnMeta[]`. |
| `Form` | Conform and Zod form wrapper. It POSTs to a route and shows field errors. |
| `useFormContext` | Reads the current `Form`'s conform metadata; throws outside a `Form`. |
| `FormField` | One labeled input, switched on its `type` prop (see below). |
| `FormError` | Renders the form-level error from `useFormContext`. |
| `FormSection` | Labeled fieldset grouping for `AutoForm`/`Form` fields. |
| `FormSubmit` | Submit button that reflects the form's pending state. |
| `confirmLeave` | `confirmLeave(proceed)` runs `proceed` now, or after the reader agrees to drop a form's unsaved changes. Call it before your own navigation or drawer close; links in the admin already go through it. |
| `AsyncSelect` | Debounced async-search select, used by reference fields. |
| `ResolvedField` (type) | The server-resolved field shape `AutoForm` consumes. |

| `cancelHref?` | `string` | Renders a cancel link back to this record or its list. It never submits. |

The table above is exported as `FormField` and `FormFieldProps`. Its `type` accepts:

```ts fragment
"text" | "email" | "password" | "url" | "number" | "date" | "datetime" |
"datetime-local" | "time" | "color" | "search" | "textarea" | "markdown" |
"json" | "tags" | "select" | "multiselect" | "radio" | "reference" |
"boolean" | "switch" | "checkbox" | "hidden"
```

The union is not exported; use `ComponentProps<typeof FormField>["type"]`.

### Widgets

| Export | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `MetricCard`, `DefaultMetricCard` | Renders a `metric()` widget and its default look. `plain` drops the card frame for a strip cell. |

| `StatGroupCard` | Renders a `statGroup()` widget. |
| `KvCard` | Renders a `kv()` widget as a label/value grid. `long` items span the card and fold the rest under `more`. |
| `BarsCard` | Renders a `bars()` widget, sizing each bar against `max` or the largest row. |
| `FunnelCard` | Renders a `funnel()` widget, deriving each step's share and drop-off and marking the worst drop past `alertDrop` in `warn`. |
| `ListCard`, `ListBanner` | Renders a `list()` widget as a short feed, or with `variant: "banner"` as a severity-ordered strip with glyphs, a "N more" line and an all-clear line. |
| `TrackerCard` | Renders a `tracker()` widget: a toned dot, one block per hour or day, and a summary per row. |
| `TimelineCard` | Renders a `timeline()` widget: kind chips, day groups, folded lines in `<details>`, and paging, all as links. |
| `HeatmapCard` | Renders a `heatmap()` widget: weeks of day cells shaded by quartile, month and weekday labels, a legend and a summary. |
| `ChecklistCard` | Renders a `checklist()` widget: a mark per item, dates and gaps when ordered, and a summary bar. |
| `TableWidget` | Renders a `table()` widget, reusing `DataTable`. |
| `CaptionLine` | The line under a card title: a cut range, how fresh the data is, or its coverage, with a ▲ when stale. |
| `CardHeading` | A card's title and caption; renders nothing when it has neither. |
| `ExpiredCard` | A widget whose whole range is older than its data is kept: its title, `—`, and why. |
| `DashboardRefresh` | Re-renders a dashboard on its `refresh` interval and stamps the numbers' age. |
| `CustomWidget` | Wraps a `custom()` widget's component with the shared widget frame. |

### Hooks

All hooks are client-only.

**`useLiveChannel(channel, onMessage, options?)`** subscribes to one SSE channel and
hands you each payload. Under `RealtimeProvider` (every admin page) it joins the admin's
one `EventSource` and does not refresh the route; without a provider, hooks on the same
endpoint share one. It returns a `RealtimeStatus` (`LiveStatus` is the same type under
its 0.3 name): `idle`, `connecting`, `live` once the server's first frame arrives,
`reconnecting` from the first error until a frame arrives again, or `offline` once
failures have lasted 30 seconds (retries continue). A stream the server ends on purpose reconnects
without leaving `live`.

```tsx
const status = useLiveChannel("resource.orders", (payload) => {
  console.log("order event", payload);
});
```

**`useAdminTable()`** reads and writes the list URL state (`?page=`, `?pageSize=`,
`?q=`, `?sort=field:dir`, `?f_<field>=`). `pageSize` is `null` when the URL sets
none. Setters use `router.replace`.

```tsx
const { page, pageSize, sort, setPage, setSort } = useAdminTable();
```

**`useUrlState()`** reads and writes typed search params.

**`useTheme(options?)`** returns the theme and `toggle`/`setTheme`, stored in
`localStorage`.

```tsx
const { theme, toggle } = useTheme();
```

**`useToast()`** fires a toast under `ToastProvider` or `FlowpanelGlobals`.

```tsx
const toast = useToast();
toast.success("Saved");
```

**`useOptimisticAction(serverValue, applyPatch)`** wraps `useOptimistic` and
`useTransition` for an optimistic value with a pending flag.

**`useAdminCommand()`** controls the ⌘K palette.

**`useAdminDrawer()`** reads and writes `?drawer=<resource>:<id>` and `?drawerTab=`.

**`useDashboardParam(key, schema, fallback)`** reads and writes one dashboard
search param, validated by a Zod schema.

**`useRowNavigation()`** returns the navigation a clicked row performs.

**`useRowHrefClick(rows, rowHrefs)`** is a `DataTable` `onRowClick` for per-row
hrefs; a `null` entry is inert.

**`useMediaQuery(query)`** subscribes to a media query, `false` on the server.
`DataTable` switches to cards at `(max-width: 639px)`.

```tsx
const isMobile = useMediaQuery("(max-width: 639px)");
```

### Realtime

**`RealtimeProvider`** mounts one shared `EventSource` for its descendants and
coalesces their refreshes. `Flowpanel` mounts it in every shell mode, `"bare"`
included. Mount it yourself only around components rendered outside that page.

**`useRealtimeRefresh(channels, options?)`** runs a debounced `router.refresh()`
on any event on its channels.

```tsx
useRealtimeRefresh("resource.orders");
```

**`RealtimeRefresh`** is the same as a component that renders nothing.

```tsx
<RealtimeRefresh channels={["resource.orders", "scraper:tick"]} />
```

**`DevToolsPanel`** shows realtime status, channels and event count in
development; it renders `null` in production.

```tsx
{process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production" && <DevToolsPanel />}
```

`DevToolsPanelProps`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen?` | `boolean` | Initial open state of the panel. Default `false`. |

Lower level: `useRealtimeBus`, `useRealtimeStatus`, `useRealtimeStats`.

### Theme utilities

Helpers behind `useTheme` and `ThemeScript`.

| Export | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `resolveTheme`, `readStoredTheme`, `writeStoredTheme`, `THEME_STORAGE_KEY` | Resolve the effective theme from storage + system preference, and read/write the stored choice. |
| `applyThemeClass`, `toggleTheme` | Apply a theme class to `<html>`, and flip the stored choice. |
| `buildThemeInitScript` | Builds the inline script string `ThemeScript` renders. |

Also exported: `cn`, `formatNumber`, `humanize`, `resolveFieldLabel`,
`triggerDownload`, `withDeploymentBasePath` (prefixes a Next.js `basePath`),
`StandaloneFormFields` (form controls outside a schema-driven `<Form>`), the
`CardDate` type (a serialized date a card renders through `LocalTime`), and `toneTextClass` and `toneFillClass` (also in `@flowpanel/kit`
for server components).

### Name collisions with `@flowpanel/kit`

These names are different declarations in `@flowpanel/kit` and here; alias one
when importing both.

| Name | In `@flowpanel/kit` | In `@flowpanel/kit/react` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TableWidget` | The `table()` builder's return **type** (`{ kind: "table"; options }`). | The **component** that renders one. |
| `CustomWidget` | The `custom()` builder's return **type**. | The **component** that wraps one. |
| `DrawerWidth` | `DrawerConfig["width"]`, the config option. | `DrawerProps["width"]`, the component prop: the same union, declared separately. |

```ts
import type { TableWidget } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import { TableWidget as TableWidgetRenderer } from "@flowpanel/kit/react";
```

`FormActionResult` is declared here and in `@flowpanel/kit/next` with identical
members.

### UI primitives

`Dialog`, `Popover`, `Select`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tabs*`, `Button`, `Checkbox`,
`Input`, `Label`, `Skeleton` and `Switch` are shadcn components with their upstream
APIs. `buttonVariants` and `DefaultButton` accompany `Button`.

## Next.js runtime

createFlowpanel, generated pages, route handlers, protected controllers and realtime helpers.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/next-runtime

Documented types: createFlowpanel, Flowpanel, FlowpanelOptions, flowpanelMetadata, handlers, stream, ApplyActionResultOptions, ResourceActions, MakeActionsOptions, FormActionResult, requestWidgetContext, RequestWidgetContextOptions, resolveWidget

`@flowpanel/kit/next` binds a config to the admin page, HTTP handlers, protected
controllers, client metadata and realtime publisher.

### createFlowpanel

Create one module-level runtime and reuse it from your route files:

```ts
// src/flowpanel.ts
import { createFlowpanel } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "../flowpanel.config";

export const flowpanel = createFlowpanel(config);
```

```ts
// src/app/admin/[[...slug]]/page.tsx
import { flowpanel } from "@/flowpanel";

export const generateMetadata = flowpanel.metadata;
export default flowpanel.page;
```

```ts
// src/app/api/flowpanel/[...route]/route.ts
import { flowpanel } from "@/flowpanel";

export const { GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS } = flowpanel.handlers;
```

`createFlowpanel(definition)` returns a frozen `FlowpanelRuntime`:

| Member | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `page` | Generated catch-all page component. |
| `metadata` | The page's `generateMetadata`: a `title` per dashboard, list, record (named by the record itself) and form ("New user", "Edit user"), or the sign-in or access-denied wall's, and `noindex`. |
| `notFound` | The admin's not-found page, titled "Page not found": `export default flowpanel.notFound;` in `not-found.tsx`. It keeps the admin's navigation; a missing record says "This customer doesn't exist or was deleted" and links back to its list. It answers 404, or 200 under `cacheComponents`, where Next has already streamed the static shell. |
| `notFoundMetadata` | The not-found page's metadata, "Page not found" and `noindex`: `export const metadata = flowpanel.notFoundMetadata;` in `not-found.tsx` titles the server's HTML, not only the page after it loads. |
| `handlers` | `FlowpanelHandlers` for REST and generated-UI routes. |
| `request()` | Current request's protected `FlowpanelRequest`. |
| `client` | Serializable `FlowpanelClientMetadata` for `@flowpanel/kit/client`. |
| `events.publish(channel, payload?)` | Namespaced, validated realtime event. |
| `dispose()` | Stops this runtime's `events.publish`. Idempotent. The process-wide publisher stays open for other runtimes. |

`events.publish` payloads must serialize to `WireValue` and stay under 64 KiB.
`FlowpanelClientMetadata` holds only paths and protocol data.

#### Protected request controllers

`await flowpanel.request()` authenticates once and returns a `FlowpanelRequest`
with a typed `ResourceController<Row>` per resource (`resource(name)` for a
dynamic name), `dashboard(path).action(key, input?)` for a dashboard action, and
the `requestId`. `ResourceListOptions<Row>` takes page, page size, search, filters,
sort, projection and soft-delete visibility. `includeDeleted` shows deleted rows
only to a user the resource's `update` rule admits, as the list's toggle does. A
deleted row read by its id (`get`, the record page, the drawer) follows the same
rule: that user sees it marked deleted, with Restore, and anyone else gets not
found.

```ts
import { flowpanel } from "@/flowpanel";

const request = await flowpanel.request();
const result = await request.resources.orders.list({
  pageSize: 25,
  select: ["id", "status", "total"],
  sort: { field: "createdAt", dir: "desc" },
});
```

Controllers return a `FlowpanelResult` for access, validation and not-found
failures, and apply the same policies, projection, scope and write pipeline as the
generated UI. Do not reuse a `FlowpanelRequest` across requests.

### Flowpanel

`Flowpanel(config)` is the page factory behind `createFlowpanel(config).page`. A
wrapper must forward both `params` and `searchParams`. The catch-all is the `slug`
param, else `rest`, else the first array-valued param, whatever the folder is named.

```ts
// src/app/admin/[[...slug]]/page.tsx
import { Flowpanel } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "../../../../flowpanel.config";

export default Flowpanel(config);
```

`FlowpanelOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shell?` | `ShellConfig \| ShellMode` | Override `config.shell` at render time. |

#### flowpanelMetadata

`flowpanelMetadata(config)` is the page's `generateMetadata`: a title per
dashboard, list and record, and `robots: noindex`. Leave `viewport.themeColor`
unset on the admin layout; the page renders its own.

```ts
// src/app/admin/[[...slug]]/page.tsx
import { Flowpanel, flowpanelMetadata } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "../../../../flowpanel.config";

export const generateMetadata = flowpanelMetadata(config);
export default Flowpanel(config);
```

`FlowpanelContent(config, opts?)` is `Flowpanel(config, { ...opts, shell: "bare" })`,
for embedding the admin in your own chrome.

### handlers

`handlers(config)` is the handler factory behind `createFlowpanel(config).handlers`:

```ts
// src/app/api/flowpanel/[...route]/route.ts
import { handlers } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "../../../../../flowpanel.config";

export const { GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS } = handlers(config);
```

Each method is a `RouteHandler`, `(request, context) => Promise<Response>`.

#### The routes it mounts

All paths are relative to `/api/flowpanel`.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/<resource>` | Typed list result for custom clients |
| `GET` | `/<resource>/<id>` | One projected row |
| `POST` | `/<resource>` | Create (JSON API) |
| `PATCH` / `PUT` | `/<resource>/<id>` | Update (JSON API) |
| `DELETE` | `/<resource>/<id>` | Delete (JSON API) |
| `GET` | `/drawer/<resource>/<id>` | Drawer payload for one row |
| `GET` | `/<resource>/reference/<field>` | Options for a reference picker |
| `GET` | `/palette/search?q=` | ⌘K record search across the resources with `search` fields ([Search](/docs/build/resources#search-filters-and-sorting)) |
| `GET` | `/export/<resource>?format=csv` | Every row the list would show for its query string, as CSV or JSON ([Import and export](/docs/build/import-export#export)) |
| `POST` | `/<resource>/create` | Create form submit |
| `POST` | `/<resource>/<id>/edit` | Edit form submit |
| `POST` | `/<resource>/<id>/update` | Inline cell edit |
| `POST` | `/<resource>/<id>/restore` | Undo a soft delete |
| `POST` | `/<resource>/import` | CSV / JSON import |
| `POST` | `/<resource>/<id>/actions/<action>` | Row action |
| `POST` | `/<resource>/bulk-actions/<action>` | Bulk action |
| `POST` | `/drawer/<resource>/<id>/actions/<action>` | Drawer action |
| `POST` | `/dashboards/<path>/actions/<action>` | Dashboard action |

Each runs, in order: the same-origin check for writes, the admin role gate and
rate limit, read-only mode for writes, the lookup of what the URL names, the
resource gate and its `access`, a dashboard's `access`, and the action's `access`.
Nothing is looked up before the caller is identified, so a refused caller gets
the same answer for a name that exists and one that does not. Every write then
takes the same path: the row read through the tenant scope, the field rules,
the write, one audit event and the realtime publish.

### stream

The SSE endpoint for realtime, on its own route.

```ts
export function stream(
  config: ResolvedAdminConfig,
  opts?: StreamOptions,
): (req: Request) => Promise<Response>;
```

`StreamOptions.heartbeatMs` sets the keep-alive interval, 15 s by default.
`maxPerActor` caps the streams one user holds at once, 10 by default, and
`maxAgeMs` ends a stream after 15 minutes so the browser reconnects through
`auth.access` again.

```ts
// src/app/api/flowpanel/stream/route.ts
import { stream } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "../../../../../flowpanel.config";

export const GET = stream(config);
```

`flowpanel init` writes this file.

#### What the stream checks

Like every route, the stream is gated by `auth.access`; without it, it is
open ([AuthConfig](/docs/reference/define-config#authconfig)). A failed role check
answers `403`. Per connection:

| Limit | Value | Behavior when exceeded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Channels per connection | 25 | Extra `?channel=` values are dropped, not rejected |
| Channel name charset | `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$/` | Non-matching names are silently ignored |
| Per-resource role gate | `resource.<name>` channels | Dropped when the resource is not registered or its `access.read` rejects the caller |
| Your own channels | any other name | Dropped unless `realtime.channels` declares it and its `access` admits the caller; development logs the name |
| Access rule that throws | any channel | That channel is dropped, the error goes to `hooks.onError`, and the stream stays open for the rest |
| Tenant scope | `resource.<name>` of a resource with `scope` | Each event carries only its `action`, never a row id or row data |
| Tenant scope | your own channel, under an admin-wide `scope` | Each event carries `{}` unless the channel is `tenantSafe` |
| Streams per user | 10 (`maxPerActor`) | The next one answers `429`; keyed by user id, else IP |
| Stream age | 15 min (`maxAgeMs`) | The response ends and the browser reconnects through auth |
| Heartbeat | 15s (`heartbeatMs`) | A `: keep-alive` comment keeps proxies from closing the response |

A channel that never receives events was probably dropped by one of the first
five rows. Right after `ready`, the stream sends `event: refused` with
`{ "channels": [...] }`, naming every channel it dropped.

### Realtime helpers

```ts
function publish(channel: string, payload?: unknown): Promise<void>;
function publishResource(
  name: string,
  event: { action: "create" | "update" | "delete"; id?: string },
): Promise<void>;
function subscribe(channel: string, handler: (payload: unknown) => void): () => void;
function bindPublisher(config: ResolvedAdminConfig): void;
```

`publishResource(name, event)` publishes on `resource.<name>`, the channel a
`realtime: true` resource listens on:

```ts
import { publishResource } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";

export async function orderShipped(order: { id: number }): Promise<void> {
  await publishResource("orders", { action: "update", id: String(order.id) });
}
```

In an action, use `ctx.publish`. `handlers`, `Flowpanel` and `stream` call
`bindPublisher` for you; call it in your own route handlers. A worker uses
[`@flowpanel/kit/publish`](/docs/guides/realtime#publish-from-a-worker).

`publish`, `publishResource`, `bindPublisher` and `emitAudit` come from
`@flowpanel/kit/next`; `requireAccess` and the request-context accessors from
`@flowpanel/kit`. Publishing before `bindPublisher` runs uses an in-memory
publisher and warns once. `emitAudit(config, event)` records an event wherever
the admin's audit log writes.

`requireAccess(rule, ctx)` throws `FlowpanelAccessError` when an `AccessRule`
rejects the context, and a missing rule denies, so a server action can reuse the
admin's rules:

```ts
import { getRequestContext, requireAccess } from "@flowpanel/kit";

await requireAccess(["admin", "support"], getRequestContext());
```

### Route handlers

Factories for single [routes](#the-routes-it-mounts), for mounting one on your
own path. Each takes `ResolvedAdminConfig` and returns a handler.

| Factory | Route |
| --- | --- |
| `resourceCreateRoute` | `POST /<resource>/create` |
| `resourceUpdateRoute` | `POST /<resource>/<id>/edit` |
| `rowActionRoute` | `POST /<resource>/<id>/actions/<action>` |
| `bulkActionRoute` | `POST /<resource>/bulk-actions/<action>` |
| `dashboardActionRoute` | `POST /dashboards/<path>/actions/<action>` |
| `drawerActionRoute` | `POST /drawer/<resource>/<id>/actions/<action>` |
| `drawerRoute` | `GET /drawer/<resource>/<id>` |
| `inlineUpdateRoute` | `POST /<resource>/<id>/update`, for `editable: true` columns |

Reference search, import and restore have no factory; they come only with
`handlers(config)`.

#### Serialization pairs

Action routes serialize actions for the client without server-only fields:

| Config type | Serializer | Wire type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RowAction` | `serializeRowAction` | `SerializedRowAction` |
| `BulkAction` | `serializeBulkAction` | `SerializedBulkAction` |
| `DashboardAction` | `serializeDashboardAction` | `SerializedDashboardAction` |
| Drawer action | none, inline in `drawerRoute` | `SerializedDrawerAction` |
| Drawer tab | none, inline in `drawerRoute` | `SerializedDrawerTab` |

`SerializedDashboardAction.form` is a `SerializedDashboardActionField[]`.

### applyActionResult

Applies a successful `ActionResult`: publishes to the channels `refresh` names (or
the resource's channel for `refresh: true`), then revalidates `pathname` unless
`refresh` is `false`. Action routes call it; call it from your own route.

`ApplyActionResultOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resourceName?` | `string` |  |
| `pathname?` | `string \| readonly string[]` | The page, or pages, whose cache the change makes stale. |
| `change?` | `{ action: "create" \| "update" \| "delete"; id?: string }` | A change FlowPanel made itself, published on `resource.<resourceName>` whatever `refresh` says. |

### Dashboard path encoding

```ts
function encodeDashboardPath(path: string): string;
function decodeDashboardPath(encoded: string): string;
```

Encodes a dashboard `path` as the one URL segment `dashboardActionRoute` expects.

### makeActions

The create, update and delete pipeline the form routes use, with the resource's
schema, field rules, scope and audit.

```ts
function makeActions(
  config: ResolvedAdminConfig,
  resource: ResourceConfig,
  opts?: MakeActionsOptions,
): ResourceActions;
```

`ResourceActions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create` | `(input: unknown, options?: CreateOptions) => Promise<unknown>` |  |
| `update` | `(id: string, input: unknown, options?: UpdateOptions) => Promise<unknown>` |  |
| `delete` | `(id: string) => Promise<void>` |  |

`MakeActionsOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reqCtx?` | `RequestContext` | Reuse a caller-built `RequestContext` instead of building one per call. |
| `publish?` | `boolean` | Publish + revalidate per call. Default `true`; set `false` to batch-notify once yourself. |
| `fromForm?` | `boolean` | The input is a posted form, which also carries the fields it showed read-only. |

The create and edit form routes answer with a `FormActionResult`:

`FormActionResult`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `boolean` |  |
| `createdKey?` | `string` | Stable row key returned by create routes so the destination list can animate that row. |
| `error?` | `string` |  |
| `fieldErrors?` | `Record<string, string>` |  |

Pass `reqCtx` to reuse a request context you already built.

### buildRequestContext

Builds the `RequestContext`. It enforces `auth.access` and the rate limit, so
it throws `FlowpanelAccessError` or `FlowpanelRateLimitError`:

```ts
// src/app/api/me/route.ts
import { FlowpanelError, type RequestContext } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import { buildRequestContext } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "../../../../flowpanel.config";

export async function GET(req: Request): Promise<Response> {
  let reqCtx: RequestContext;
  try {
    reqCtx = await buildRequestContext({ req, config });
  } catch (err) {
    if (!(err instanceof FlowpanelError)) throw err;
    return Response.json({ ok: false, error: err.safeMessage }, { status: err.status });
  }
  return Response.json({ ok: true, requestId: reqCtx.requestId });
}
```

### Widget contexts

`RequestWidgetContextOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `range?` | `{ from: Date; to: Date; preset?: DateRangePreset }` | The picked period; its previous period follows. Default: `the whole history until now`. |
| `row?` | `Record<string, unknown>` | The viewed record, for a record-page widget. |
| `resource?` | `string` | The resource `row` belongs to: its `rowKey` names `ctx.id`, and `ctx.rowOf` checks it. |
| `filters?` | `Readonly<Record<string, string>>` | The dashboard filters widgets read as `ctx.filters`. Default: `{}`. |

The context a widget receives for one request, under that request's session, role
and scope, for running a widget outside a page.

Runs a widget as a dashboard does and returns its `kind` and props.

For tests, `adminWidgetContext(config, options)` and `widgetContext()` from
`@flowpanel/kit/test/widgets` build a context with no request and no tenant scope,
with the role `"admin"` unless you pass another. They are not exported from
`@flowpanel/kit/next`, so a page cannot use them by mistake; see
[Testing](/docs/reference/testing#unit-test-a-widget).

### Navigation

```ts
function buildNav(config: ResolvedAdminConfig, reqCtx?: RequestContext): Promise<NavGroup[]>;
function resourceNavName(resource: ResourceConfig): string;
```

`buildNav` resolves to the sidebar entries, for your own chrome around a `"bare"`
shell. Pass `reqCtx` to apply each entry's `access`, or a resource's `access.read`. `resourceNavName` returns
a resource's resolved name and throws if it cannot.

## Typed client

Call the protected FlowPanel HTTP API from custom React UI, then add mutation state where needed.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/client

Documented types: createFlowpanelClient, UseAdminMutation, UseAdminMutationOptions

`@flowpanel/kit/client` calls the admin's HTTP API from custom browser UI. Calls go
through the same auth, access, scope, validation and audit as generated pages.

```ts
import {
  createFlowpanelClient,
  isFlowpanelErrorCode,
  isFlowpanelErrorResult,
  type CreateFlowpanelClientOptions,
  type FlowpanelClient,
  type FlowpanelClientMetadata,
  type FlowpanelFetchOptions,
  type FlowpanelListOptions,
  type FlowpanelResourceClient,
} from "@flowpanel/kit/client";
```

### Create a client

The client needs the runtime's metadata: `createFlowpanel(config).client`. Read it in a Server Component and pass it to the client component as a prop, so the config, adapter and database client stay on the server:

```tsx
// src/app/orders/page.tsx
import { createFlowpanel } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "../../../flowpanel.config";
import { OrdersPanel } from "./orders-panel";

const flowpanel = createFlowpanel(config);

export default function OrdersPage() {
  return <OrdersPanel metadata={flowpanel.client} />;
}
```

```tsx
// src/app/orders/orders-panel.tsx
"use client";

import { createFlowpanelClient, type FlowpanelClientMetadata } from "@flowpanel/kit/client";
import type { orders } from "@/db/schema";

type Order = typeof orders.$inferSelect;

export function OrdersPanel({ metadata }: { metadata: FlowpanelClientMetadata }) {
  async function loadOpenOrders() {
    const orders = createFlowpanelClient(metadata).resource<Order>("orders");
    const result = await orders.list({
      page: 1,
      pageSize: 25,
      search: "acme",
      filters: { status: "open" },
    });
    if (!result.ok) console.error(result.error.code, result.error.message);
  }
  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={loadOpenOrders}>
      Load open orders
    </button>
  );
}
```

`options.fetch` replaces the fetch implementation. Requests use
`credentials: "same-origin"`. `FlowpanelClientMetadata` holds the runtime id, paths
and protocol version; it is not secret.

### Resource methods

`client.resource<Row>(name)` returns a `FlowpanelResourceClient<Row>`:

| Method | HTTP request | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list(options?)` | `GET /<resource>` | Paginated rows |
| `get(id, options?)` | `GET /<resource>/<id>` | One projected row |
| `create(input, options?)` | `POST /<resource>` | Created row |
| `update(id, input, options?)` | `PATCH /<resource>/<id>` | Updated row |
| `delete(id, options?)` | `DELETE /<resource>/<id>` | `null` on success |

`FlowpanelListOptions` takes `page`, `pageSize`, `search` and `filters`; every call
takes `signal` and `headers`. Network errors and malformed responses become an
`internal` failure; an `AbortError` is rethrown.

### Narrowing errors

`isFlowpanelErrorResult(result)` narrows to the error branch;
`isFlowpanelErrorCode(value)` checks a code.

```ts
import {
  createFlowpanelClient,
  type FlowpanelClientMetadata,
  isFlowpanelErrorCode,
  isFlowpanelErrorResult,
} from "@flowpanel/kit/client";

export async function shipOrder(metadata: FlowpanelClientMetadata, id: string): Promise<void> {
  const orders = createFlowpanelClient(metadata).resource("orders");
  const result = await orders.update(id, { status: "shipped" });
  if (isFlowpanelErrorResult(result) && result.error.code === "field_forbidden") {
    // Hide or disable the corresponding control.
  }
}

isFlowpanelErrorCode("rate_limited"); // true
isFlowpanelErrorCode("anything"); // false
```

### Mutation state hook

`useAdminMutation` tracks pending and error state for an async function that resolves to an `ActionResult` (`{ ok: true, ... }` or `{ ok: false, error }`).

```tsx
// src/app/orders/archive-button.tsx
"use client";
import { useAdminMutation } from "@flowpanel/kit/client";
import { archiveOrder } from "./actions";

export function ArchiveButton({ id }: { id: string }) {
  const { run, pending, error, reset } = useAdminMutation(archiveOrder);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => run(id)} disabled={pending}>
        Archive
      </button>
      {error ? <button onClick={reset}>{error}</button> : null}
    </>
  );
}
```

`UseAdminMutation`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | `(...args: Args) => Promise<ActionResult>` |  |
| `pending` | `boolean` |  |
| `error` | `string \| null` |  |
| `reset` | `() => void` |  |

`UseAdminMutationOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onSuccess?` | `(result: Extract<ActionResult, { ok: true }>) => void` |  |
| `onError?` | `(message: string) => void` |  |

`run` never throws: a rejection sets `error` to its message, and `{ ok: false, error }` sets `error` to that string. `reset()` clears
it. For optimistic values, see [`useOptimisticAction`](/docs/reference/react-components#hooks).

## Runtime contracts

Low-level policy, result, adapter and pipeline APIs for custom runtimes and third-party adapters.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/runtime-contracts

Lower-level contracts from `@flowpanel/kit` for adapter authors and custom
integrations. An app built with `defineAdmin` and `createFlowpanel` does not need
them.

```ts
import {
  accessAllows,
  assertWritableInput,
  bindAdapterScope,
  resolveScopeApplier,
  errorResult,
  filterReadableProjection,
  reportUnexpectedError,
  requireAccess,
  resolveOperationAccess,
  resultResponse,
  FLOWPANEL_ERROR_STATUS,
  type AccessContext,
  type AccessRule,
  type AdminDefinition,
  type AdminPaths,
  type AdminPathsInput,
  type AnyResourceConfig,
  type AdapterScopeContext,
  type BoundAdapterScope,
  type ErrorContext,
  type FieldAccess,
  type FieldAccessMap,
  type FieldWriteContext,
  type FlowpanelErrorCode,
  type FlowpanelResult,
  type FlowpanelResultError,
  type FlowpanelResultMeta,
  type FlowpanelWarning,
  type FlowpanelWarningCode,
  type JsonValue,
  type ResourceAccess,
  type ResourceOperation,
} from "@flowpanel/kit";
```

### Definitions and paths

`AdminDefinition<Resources>` is the immutable public input accepted by
`defineAdmin`; `AnyResourceConfig` is its generic resource constraint.
`AdminPathsInput` is the partial `{ admin, api }` input and `AdminPaths` is the
normalized resolved pair. Both paths have a leading slash and no trailing
slash.

Useful when a factory returns a definition:

```ts
function companyAdmin(): AdminDefinition {
  return {
    adapter,
    auth: flowpanelAuth,
    paths: { admin: "/ops", api: "/api/ops" },
  };
}
```

### Access and field policy

`AccessRule` is a boolean, role string, role list, or predicate receiving
`AccessContext` (`session`, `role`, `scope`). `ResourceAccess` maps those rules
to the four `ResourceOperation` values: `read`, `create`, `update`, `delete`.

- `accessAllows(rule, context)` evaluates one normalized rule.
- `resolveOperationAccess(access, operation)` returns the rule `access` sets for
  that operation, or `undefined` when it sets none.
- `requireAccess(rule, context)` throws the safe access error when the rule rejects
  the request. It takes a rule, and a missing one denies; pass `true` to allow
  everyone.

`FieldAccess<Row>` adds `read`, `write` and `sensitive` policy. A
`FieldAccessMap<Row>` maps it by field name; write predicates receive
`FieldWriteContext<Row>` with both the current row and submitted input.

- `filterReadableProjection(fields, policy, context)` removes fields the
  caller may not read before the adapter query is built.
- `assertWritableInput({ declaredFields, policies, input, context })` resolves to
  the input as `Partial<Row>`. It throws on an unknown, sensitive or forbidden
  field; it never drops one silently.

### Bound adapter scope

A tenant policy crosses the runtime/adapter boundary as an opaque
`BoundAdapterScope`. Create it with `bindAdapterScope(apply)`. Adapters must
apply it to list, get, update and delete operations and fail closed when the
bound predicate leaves the query unconstrained.

`resolveScopeApplier(ctx)` returns the bound predicate, or `null` when the
resource declares none. The first-party adapters throw `FlowpanelAccessError`
when the predicate adds no condition; an adapter that applies scope by hand must
refuse the query in the same case.

Create and update must also leave the row inside the scope. The first-party
adapters throw `FlowpanelAccessError` and write nothing when the new or changed
row would fall outside it, such as an update that sets the tenant column to
another tenant. A custom adapter must do the same.

### Post-commit effects

Post-commit audit, realtime or revalidation failures do not turn a committed
mutation into a false failure. Each is logged on the server with `console.error`
(`[flowpanel] audit write failed`, `realtime effect failed`, `revalidation effect
failed`) and the response reports the write as done.

### Result envelope

Every protected controller and v1 JSON CRUD endpoint returns
`FlowpanelResult<T>`:

```ts
type FlowpanelResult<T> =
  | { ok: true; data: T; meta: FlowpanelResultMeta }
  | { ok: false; error: FlowpanelResultError };
```

`FlowpanelResultMeta` carries the request id and optional warnings.
`FlowpanelResultError` carries a stable `FlowpanelErrorCode`, a safe message,
optional field errors and request id. `FLOWPANEL_ERROR_STATUS` is the canonical
code-to-HTTP-status table.

- `errorResult(error, requestId)` converts known errors to the envelope and
  redacts unexpected failures to `internal`.
- `resultResponse(result)` produces a JSON `Response` with the canonical status.
- `reportUnexpectedError(error, context, onError)` invokes `hooks.onError` at
  most once for the same error object, and skips a `FlowpanelError` entirely.
  Without `onError` it logs the error once with `console.error` and the request id. `ErrorContext` includes request,
  operation, actor, IP and user-agent diagnostics but no submitted secrets.

An action should throw a FlowPanel error or return an `ActionResult` rather than
build the envelope. The generated form, drawer, action, import, restore and SSE
routes use their own compact responses; use `createFlowpanelClient` for the
envelope above.

## Adapter contract

What FlowPanel needs from a database layer, method by method.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/adapters

Documented types: Adapter, AuditLogStore, ResourceIntrospection, ColumnMeta, drizzleAdapter, prismaAdapter, bullmqAdapter, DrizzleAdapterOptions, PrismaAdapterOptions

The adapter is the only part of FlowPanel that queries your database. Implement
this interface for a data layer without a shipped adapter. Overview:
[Adapters and introspection](/docs/understand/adapters).

Shipped adapters: [`drizzleAdapter`](/docs/introduction/drizzle) and
[`prismaAdapter`](/docs/introduction/prisma).

### Adapter

`Adapter`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `AdapterKind` | Which ORM this adapter wraps. Shipped adapters use `"drizzle"` / `"prisma"`. |
| `db` | `DB` | The client handed to every `ctx.db`. |
| `transaction?` | `(run: (db: DB) => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>` | Execute work against one transaction-bound database handle. |
| `introspect` | `(ref: Ref) => ResourceIntrospection` | Describe a table: its columns, types and primary key. |
| `inferSchema` | `(ref: Ref) => { create: z.ZodTypeAny; update: z.ZodTypeAny; select: z.ZodTypeAny; }` | Derive validation schemas from the table, used when a resource sets no `schema`. |
| `list` | `(ref: Ref, ctx: ListQueryContext<unknown>) => Promise<ListResult<unknown>>` | One page of rows, honoring filters, sort, search, scope and soft delete. |
| `get` | `(ref: Ref, ctx: ItemQueryContext) => Promise<unknown \| null>` | A single row by id, or null. Must respect tenant scope. |
| `create` | `(ref: Ref, ctx: MutationContext<unknown>) => Promise<unknown>` | Insert a row. Must reject rows that fall outside the caller's scope. |
| `update` | `(ref: Ref, ctx: MutationContext<unknown>) => Promise<unknown \| null>` | Update a row by id, or return null when it does not exist in scope. |
| `delete` | `(ref: Ref, ctx: MutationContext<unknown>) => Promise<void>` | Delete a row — or stamp `ctx.softDelete.column` when soft delete is on. |
| `restore?` | `(ref: Ref, ctx: MutationContext<unknown>) => Promise<void>` | Clear the soft-delete stamp. Without it, the admin hides the restore button. |
| `sql?` | `(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]) => Promise<Row[]>` | Runs one read-only statement and returns its rows, as a tagged template; every value arrives as a bound parameter. Without it, `ctx.sql` throws. |
| `count?` | `(ref: Ref, where?: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<number>` | Counts matching rows without reading them; `where` is the same filter shape `list` receives. Without it, FlowPanel counts through `list` with an empty projection instead. |
| `applyMigration?` | `(id: string, sql: string) => Promise<void>` | Optional migration support, used by `flowpanel migrate`. A concurrent-safe implementation must serialize and recheck `id` at the database boundary. |
| `listAppliedMigrations?` | `() => Promise<Set<string>>` |  |
| `auditLog?` | `AuditLogStore` | The `flowpanel_audit_log` table that `flowpanel migrate` creates. Without it, `audit` needs a `sink`. |

`Ref` is what `resource(ref, …)` accepts; `DB` is the client widgets receive as `ctx.db`.
`kind` is a label (`"drizzle"`, `"prisma"` or your own); nothing branches on it.

`kind`, `db`, `introspect`, `inferSchema`, `list`, `get`, `create`, `update` and
`delete` are required. Without `restore`, the restore button is hidden. `sql` and
`count` back [`ctx.sql` and `ctx.count`](/docs/reference/contexts#raw-sql-and-counts).
`applyMigration(id, sql)` and `listAppliedMigrations` power `flowpanel migrate`.

`applyMigration` must serialize migrators at the database and recheck the ID under
the lock, so a concurrent duplicate is a no-op. The shipped adapters run each file
and its marker in one transaction on PostgreSQL and SQLite. On MySQL, which commits
DDL implicitly, Drizzle holds a `GET_LOCK` advisory lock and Prisma a claim row in
`_flowpanel_migration_claims` that records where a failed run stopped; later runs
stop until you repair the schema and delete that row. Both reject procedural
scripts (trigger bodies, stored procedures, `DELIMITER`) unless the body uses
PostgreSQL dollar quoting.

### Audit log

`auditLog` is the `flowpanel_audit_log` table that `0001_init.sql` creates. The
admin appends each [audit event](/docs/guides/audit-log) to it and reads the record
History tabs and the Audit log page from it. The shipped adapters bind every value
through the same client `flowpanel migrate` uses. `list` returns events newest
first; with `scope` set, only those whose stored tenant key equals `scope.key`.
`append` writes one row per id in `targetIds`. Without `auditLog`, an admin with
`audit` on needs a `sink`.

`AuditLogStore`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `append` | `(event: AuditEvent) => Promise<void>` |  |
| `list` | `(query: AuditLogQuery) => Promise<AuditLogPage>` |  |
| `facets` | `(query: Pick<AuditLogQuery, "scope" \| "visible" \| "from">) => Promise<AuditLogFacets>` | Who acted and what ran among the events `query` selects, newest actors first. |

### Raw SQL

`sql` is a tagged template: every interpolated value must reach the database as a
bound parameter, never concatenated.

`count(ref, where)` takes the `list` filter shape. FlowPanel calls it only for
unscoped resources and counts scoped ones through `list`. Both run on the
adapter's own `db`, outside any transaction or per-request session settings.

Two helpers match the shipped adapters' behaviour:

```ts
import { parseSqlRows, sanitizeSqlParams } from "@flowpanel/kit";

async function sql<Row>(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]) {
  const rows = await driver.query(strings, sanitizeSqlParams(values));
  return parseSqlRows<Row>(rows);
}
```

`sanitizeSqlParams` binds a `Date` as ISO-8601 text and a `bigint` as decimal text.
`parseSqlRows` reads zoneless `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` strings as UTC `Date`s, unless
`{ parseDates: false }`.

Arrays differ: Drizzle expands `${ids}` into a list, so `where id in (${ids})`
works; Prisma binds one parameter, so write `where id = any(${ids})` or use
`Prisma.join`.

### ResourceIntrospection

Returned by `introspect`. `kind: "view"` makes a resource read-only unless it sets
[`writeTo`](/docs/reference/resources#reading-a-view).

`ResourceIntrospection`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Table name, used as the resource's default `name`. |
| `columns` | `ColumnMeta[]` |  |
| `primaryKey` | `string` |  |
| `keyColumns?` | `readonly string[]` | Every column of a composite primary key, in order, when the adapter can see them. |
| `kind?` | `"table" \| "view"` | What the ref is. A view has no write path of its own; see `ResourceOptions.writeTo`. Default: `"table"`. |

### ColumnMeta

`ColumnMeta`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `type` | `"string" \| "number" \| "boolean" \| "date" \| "json" \| "enum" \| "array" \| "reference"` | Normalized type. Decides the default form control and filter. |
| `nullable` | `boolean` |  |
| `unique` | `boolean` |  |
| `primaryKey` | `boolean` |  |
| `integer?` | `boolean` | A `number` column that holds whole numbers only, such as `integer` or `bigint`; `false` for decimals and floats. |
| `enumValues?` | `readonly string[]` | Allowed values, for `enum` columns. |
| `references?` | `{ table: string; column: string }` | Foreign key target, when the column references another table. |
| `maxLength?` | `number` |  |
| `readable?` | `boolean` | Whether this column may be selected and returned by the adapter. |
| `writableOnCreate?` | `boolean` | Whether create input may contain this column. |
| `writableOnUpdate?` | `boolean` | Whether update input may contain this column. |
| `generated?` | `boolean` | Database-computed column that must not be accepted as input. |
| `hasDefault?` | `boolean` | The database or ORM fills the column when the insert omits it. |
| `sensitive?` | `boolean` | Adapter-discovered secret. Always excluded from generated read projections. |

`type` and `enumValues` drive a fully generated form (no `create.fields` or
`update.fields`) and editable list cells:

| Column | Generated form control | Editable cell |
| --- | --- | --- |
| has `enumValues` | `select` | text |
| `number` | `number` | `number` |
| `boolean` | `checkbox` | text |
| `date` | `datetime-local` | `datetime-local` |
| `json` | `json` | text |
| anything else | `text` | text |

Filters and declared fields do not infer a type from the column. `references` is
reported for your own use.

### What an implementation must honor

Three obligations keep the admin safe:

**Tenant scope.** When `ctx.boundScope` is set, every method must constrain
its query with `ctx.boundScope.apply`, and refuse a query the predicate leaves unconstrained. `create` and `update` included: writing or moving a row outside the
caller's scope is as much a leak as reading one.

**The search allowlist.** `list` searches only `ctx.searchFields`.

**Soft delete.** When `ctx.softDelete` is set, `list` and `get` must exclude
stamped rows unless `ctx.includeDeleted` is set, and `delete` must stamp the
column rather than remove the row.

### Adapter options

`DrizzleAdapterOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `db` | `DB` |  |
| `schema` | `Record<string, unknown>` |  |
| `dialect?` | `DrizzleDialect` | Inferred from `schema` when omitted. |
| `parseDates?` | `boolean` | Reads zoneless `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` strings as UTC `Date`s; turn off if a text column holds timestamp-shaped strings `select *` cannot cast. Default: `true`. |

`PrismaAdapterOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prisma` | `P` |  |
| `provider` | `PrismaProvider` | The `datasource` provider from schema.prisma; migrations are dialect-specific. |
| `dmmf?` | `PrismaDmmf` |  |
| `parseDates?` | `boolean` | Reads zoneless `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` strings as UTC `Date`s; turn off if a text column holds timestamp-shaped strings `select *` cannot cast. Default: `true`. |

`prismaAdapter` needs `provider`, a `PrismaProvider`: `"postgresql"`, `"mysql"` or
`"sqlite"`. An adapter may also implement `transaction(run)`; both built-in
adapters do, and the built-in bulk delete uses it so a failure deletes nothing.
On better-sqlite3 the Drizzle adapter's transaction is `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and
`COMMIT` on the shared connection: it is isolated from other transactions, but a
plain query another request runs on that connection while the transaction awaits
joins it, and rolls back with it.

`list` receives `tiebreak` when a read needs a stable order across pages, as the
export does: the key columns to order by after `sort`. They come from
`introspect().keyColumns` for a composite key (a Drizzle table-level
`primaryKey()` or a Prisma `@@id`), else the primary key when it is a real column;
a resource whose key the adapter cannot see gets none, and its export is unordered.

`bullmqAdapter` takes the queue map itself, with no options object:
`bullmqAdapter({ email: emailQueue })`.

### Also exported

The parts each adapter is built from:

| Package | Also exports |
| --- | --- |
| `@flowpanel/kit/drizzle` | `introspect`, `inferSchema` |
| `@flowpanel/kit/prisma` | `introspect`, `inferSchema`, `PrismaDmmf` (type) |
| `@flowpanel/kit/bullmq` | `BullMQAdapter` (type) |

`introspect(ref)` returns a `ResourceIntrospection`; `inferSchema(ref)` returns the
`{ create, update, select }` Zod schemas. `PrismaDmmf` is the type of the optional
`dmmf` option.

## Scope & realtime

Tenant scoping, the publisher contract, and the rate limiter.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/scope-realtime

Documented types: ScopeContext, assertResourceScope, ScopeCheckInput, Publisher, createRealtimeTransport, RealtimeChannel, createPublisher, PublisherClient, RedisLike, ResourceChange, encodeEnvelope, decodeEnvelope, RateLimiter

### Scope

A scope is resolved once per request and applied by the adapter to every query.
Guide: [Multi-tenant scope](/docs/guides/multi-tenant-scope).

```ts
type Scope = Record<string, unknown> | null;
// FlowpanelTypes["session"] when you register it, else Record<string, unknown>
type Session = Record<string, unknown>;
```

`AdminDefinition.scope` receives:

`ScopeContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `req` | `Request` |  |
| `session` | `Session \| null` |  |

```ts
scope: async ({ session }) => ({ orgId: session?.user?.orgId }),
```

The returned object reaches resource predicates as their first argument, and
policies, mutations and actions as `ctx.scope`. The adapter receives the
resource's predicate bound to it as `ctx.boundScope`. Widgets get no `ctx.scope`:
`ctx.count` and `ctx.read` apply the scope for you, and a `ctx.sql` or `ctx.db`
query must read the tenant from `ctx.session`.

Return `allTenants` from `@flowpanel/kit` for a user who works across tenants: the
resource predicates are skipped for that request, and `isAllTenants(scope)` tells
it apart. A resource's `scopeOf(row)` names the tenant a row belongs to, in the
shape `scope` returns, so the audit log files that user's changes under it.

#### The opt-out is mandatory

With a global `scope`, every resource declares its own `scope` or
`scope: "bypass"`. One that does neither throws `FlowpanelAccessError` on its first
query.

`ScopeCheckInput`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hasGlobal` | `boolean` |  |
| `resourceScope` | `"bypass" \| ResourceScope \| undefined` |  |

FlowPanel runs this check per request; call it only in your own adapter or route.

### Publisher

The realtime transport, built from `AdminDefinition.realtime` by
`createRealtimeTransport`. Implement it for another bus. Guide:
[Realtime](/docs/guides/realtime). A worker uses `createPublisher` from
`@flowpanel/kit/publish` instead.

`Publisher`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
