| `publish` | `(channel: string, payload?: unknown) => Promise<void>` |  |
| `subscribe` | `(channel: string, handler: (payload: unknown) => void) => () => void` |  |
| `close?` | `() => Promise<void>` | Release the transport's connections. Publishing afterwards throws. |

```ts
type PublisherOptions =
  | { driver: "memory" }
  | { driver: "redis"; url?: string; client?: RedisLike; keyPrefix?: string };
```

`AdminDefinition.realtime` also takes `channels`, the channels of your own the
stream may serve ([Realtime](/docs/guides/realtime#declare-your-own-channels)):

`RealtimeChannel`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Who may subscribe. Default: everyone `auth.access` admits. |
| `tenantSafe?` | `boolean` | The payload carries nothing tenant-specific. Under an admin-wide `scope`, a channel without it delivers `{}`, so subscribers only learn that something changed. Default: `false`. |

The memory driver reaches only the publishing process. The Redis driver loads the
optional `ioredis` peer on first use and needs `url` or `client`; with `client`,
FlowPanel publishes on it and calls `duplicate()` only to subscribe. Nothing
connects until the first publish or subscribe. Connection errors are logged once
per kind and never rethrown.

`keyPrefix` defaults to `"flowpanel"`, so `resource.orders` travels as
`flowpanel:resource.orders`. Use one channel per payload shape. Payloads are
JSON in every driver, so a `Date` arrives as an ISO string, and a payload that
cannot be encoded is rejected.

`close()` releases connections the publisher opened; a `client` you passed stays
open. After `close()`, `publish` throws.

#### Publishing from a worker

A worker, cron job or script imports only `@flowpanel/kit/publish` and opens one
connection.

`PublisherClient`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `publish` | `(channel: string, payload?: unknown) => Promise<void>` |  |
| `resource` | `(name: string, change?: ResourceChange) => Promise<void>` | Tell every open list and record page of the resource named `name` that its rows changed, on `resource.<name>`. |
| `channelFor` | `(resource: string) => string` | The channel a resource's own events travel on: `resource.<name>`. |
| `close` | `() => Promise<void>` | Release the connections this client opened. Idempotent; a host's client is left open. |

`RedisLike`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `publish` | `(channel: string, message: string) => Promise<unknown>` |  |
| `on` | `(event: "error", cb: (err: unknown) => void) => unknown` |  |
| `off?` | `(event: "error", cb: (err: unknown) => void) => unknown` |  |
| `removeListener?` | `(event: "error", cb: (err: unknown) => void) => unknown` |  |
| `duplicate?` | `() => unknown` | A second connection for subscribing, checked at runtime for `subscribe`, `unsubscribe` and `on`. |

`ResourceChange`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action?` | `"create" \| "update" \| "delete"` | Default: `"update"`. |
| `id?` | `string \| number` | The changed record's key, when one record changed. |

```ts
import { createPublisher } from "@flowpanel/kit/publish";

const events = createPublisher({
  redis: process.env.REDIS_URL!,
  onError: (err) => console.error("realtime publish failed", err),
});

export async function orderChanged(id: number): Promise<void> {
  await events.resource("orders", { id });
}
```

It also takes the admin's `{ driver: "redis", url, keyPrefix }` options. A
transport error resolves the call and reaches `onError`.

The SSE envelope helpers, for reading the stream without FlowPanel's client:

`decodeEnvelope` returns `null` for a frame that is not an envelope.

#### The memory driver in a Redis deployment

The publisher is bound per process from `config.realtime` and rebinds when the
options change. It warns once when the driver is `memory` while `REDIS_URL` or
`FLOWPANEL_REDIS_URL` is set:

```text
[flowpanel] realtime driver is memory while REDIS_URL is set — other instances
and workers will not receive events; set realtime: { driver: 'redis', url:
process.env.REDIS_URL } in defineAdmin
```

### RateLimiter

`RateLimiter`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check` | `(key: string) => Promise<boolean>` | Returns true if the request is allowed; false if the limit is exceeded. |

```ts
function createRateLimiter(opts: RateLimitOptions): RateLimiter;
```

`check` returns `false` over the limit, which becomes a `429`. With `per: "user"`
the key is `AuthConfig.userId`, else the session's `id` or `user.id`, else the IP.
The memory driver counts per process. The Redis driver's key prefix defaults to
`"fp:rl:"`.

## Errors

The error hierarchy, its status codes, and what reaches the operator.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/errors

Documented types: FlowpanelError, FlowpanelValidationError, FlowpanelConfigError

Throw one of these from an action, adapter or custom route and FlowPanel answers
with its status and `safeMessage`. Any other error becomes a generic `500` with no
detail in the response beyond its `requestId`.
FlowPanel passes the error to `hooks.onError`, so send it to your logger there.
Without a hook it logs one `console.error` with the operation and the same request
id. In development the log has the whole error; in production only the first line of
the error and its cause, so query parameters and the values they carry stay out of it.

### FlowpanelError

The base class. Every other error extends it.

| Property | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `code` | Stable machine-readable tag, e.g. `"validation_failed"`. |
| `safeMessage` | Shown to the operator verbatim. Keep internals out of it. |
| `status` | HTTP status from `FLOWPANEL_ERROR_STATUS[code]`. |

Construct it directly for a case the subclasses do not cover:

```ts
throw new FlowpanelError("conflict", "This order is already being processed");
```

### The subclasses

| Class | `code` | Status | Default message | Raised by FlowPanel? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FlowpanelValidationError` | `validation_failed` | 422 | Validation failed | yes |
| `FlowpanelAuthError` | `unauthenticated` | 401 | Authentication required | no, yours to throw |
| `FlowpanelAccessError` | `forbidden` | 403 | Forbidden | yes |
| `FlowpanelFieldAccessError` | `field_forbidden` | 403 | `Field "x" cannot be changed.` | yes |
| `FlowpanelOperationDisabledError` | `operation_disabled` | 403 | This operation is disabled. | yes |
| `FlowpanelUnknownFieldError` | `unknown_field` | 400 | `Unknown field: "x".` | yes |
| `FlowpanelNotFoundError` | `not_found` | 404 | Not found | yes |
| `FlowpanelConflictError` | `conflict` | 409 | Conflict | yes, for a database conflict |
| `FlowpanelRateLimitError` | `rate_limited` | 429 | Rate limit exceeded | yes |

Each takes an optional message, except the two field errors, which take the field
name, and `FlowpanelValidationError`, which takes its field errors first.

#### FlowpanelValidationError

It carries `fieldErrors`, keyed by field name, as the first constructor argument:

```ts fragment
constructor(fieldErrors: Record<string, string>, message = "Validation failed");
```

Forms show each entry beside its input.

```ts
import { FlowpanelValidationError } from "@flowpanel/kit";

throw new FlowpanelValidationError({
  email: "That address is already registered",
});

// with a banner message as well:
throw new FlowpanelValidationError({ email: "Already registered" }, "Could not save");
```

### Database constraint violations

A create, edit, inline edit or delete that breaks a database constraint does not
become a `500`. FlowPanel reads the Postgres, MySQL, SQLite or Prisma error, through
any wrapping error, and answers with a message from `labels.form`:

| Violation | Column known | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unique | yes | 422, `taken` on the field: "Email is already taken" |
| Unique | no, e.g. a composite key | 409, `conflict` |
| Foreign key on a write | yes | 422, `missingReference` on the field |
| Foreign key on a write | no | 409, `missingLink` |
| Foreign key on a delete | either | 409, `inUse` |
| NOT NULL | yes | 422, `required` on the field |

The column is matched to the resource's field by name, ignoring case and `_`, so
`user_id` reaches `userId`. A violation without a column it can match, and any
other database error, stays a `500` and is reported as above.

### FlowpanelConfigError

`defineAdmin` throws a `FlowpanelConfigError` while the config loads, so the app
fails to start. It is not a `FlowpanelError` and is never sent to the client:
one thrown during a request, such as `devAuth()` in production, becomes a `500`.
Every one reads the same way:

```text
[flowpanel] <where in the config>: <what is wrong>. <how to fix>.
```

`where` holds the config path on its own, such as `resource "orders" drawer.tabs[0]`.
The errors cover duplicate or reserved names, duplicate action keys, unknown
columns, an unintrospectable ref without `columns`, unresolved references,
`rowClick: "drawer"` without a drawer, removed options, unsafe route paths, a
production admin without real auth, and `devAuth()` in production. See
[Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting#defineadmin-throws-when-the-app-boots).

#### Did you mean

An unknown name close to a registered one gets a suggestion: a match ignoring case
and `_`/`-`, else the closest within edit distance two.

```text
[flowpanel] resource "users" columns[0]: it points at column "emial", which the
adapter does not report. Did you mean "email"? Known columns: "id", "email".
```

It covers column, filter, sort, field, tab, reference, view and link names. A link,
view or count `where` value must match its filter type: an array needs a
`multiselect` filter, `{ gte, lte }` a range filter; a bare `Date` is rejected.
Names computed at run time (function links, `ctx.count`, `ctx.read`, `ctx.rowOf`)
are checked when they run.

#### Warnings that do not stop the boot

`defineAdmin` collects non-fatal problems in `warnings`, prints each once in
development, and `flowpanel doctor` lists them. For example, a create form that
cannot succeed:

```text
resource users: create is enabled but required column `email` has no field;
creation will always fail
```

It fires for a required column with no default that neither `create.fields` nor
`create.defaultValues` fills.

### On the page render path

`FlowpanelAuthError` and `FlowpanelAccessError` thrown during a page render:

- `auth.signInUrl` is set → redirect there.
- `auth.forbiddenUrl` is set and the visitor is signed in → redirect there.
- Neither → an inline "Sign in required" or "Access denied" panel.

Other errors reach your Next.js error boundary, except failed adapter reads.

#### A query that failed

When `list` or `get` throws, FlowPanel shows a card in place of the data with the
request id the error was logged under:

```text
users: list failed
Check the column list and the database schema. Details are in the server log.
Request 5f3c…
```

Outside production the card also shows the message in a closed disclosure. A
`FlowpanelError` or a `redirect()` passes through.

#### Widget failures

A widget whose query or render throws becomes one failed card, named by title,
kind and place:

```text
«Pipeline» (custom, /system section 2 widget 1): relation "pipeline_view" does not exist
«Broken» (metric, user tab "summary" widget 1): boom
```

Outside production the card shows it in a closed disclosure; in production only
the server log and the Sentry tag `widget.id` carry it.

### Returning versus throwing

Inside an action's `run` you have both options:

```ts
run: async (row, input, ctx) => {
  if (row.status === "refunded") {
    return { ok: false, error: "Already refunded" };   // 200 with a failure body
  }
  throw new FlowpanelConflictError("Order is locked"); // 409
}
```

Return `{ ok: false }` for an outcome the operator can fix; throw when the request
itself is invalid.

### Errors the routes produce themselves

The generated UI routes (actions, forms, drawers, inline edits, import and restore) answer every failure as `{ ok: false, error, code, requestId?, fieldErrors? }`: `error` is a string to show, `code` a `FlowpanelErrorCode`, and `requestId` is set once the guards have run. Some errors come from the routes themselves:

| Status | `error` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid JSON body` | A JSON body that does not parse. |
| 400 | `JSON body must be an object` | A JSON array or scalar. |
| 400 | `invalid form data` | A form body that does not parse. |
| 413 | `request body is too large` | A body over the size limit. |
| 403 | `Cross-origin write requests are not allowed.` | The default browser origin guard blocks a mutation. |
| 403 | `This admin is read-only.` | `readOnly: true` blocks a write. |
| 422 | `too many ids (max N)` | A bulk action gets more ids than its `max`. |
| 404 | `resource not found`, `action not found`, `dashboard not found` | The route names something the config does not register, such as an action removed since the page loaded. |
| 422 | `validation failed` | An action `form` fails validation; `fieldErrors` holds one message per field. See [Actions → Validation](/docs/reference/actions#validation). |

The JSON CRUD API that the [typed client](/docs/reference/client) calls answers with
a `FlowpanelResultError`, `{ ok: false, error: { code, message } }`, instead:

| Status | `code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `bad_request` | A body that does not parse or is not a JSON object. |
| 405 | `method_not_allowed` | A method the route does not serve; `Allow` lists the ones it does. |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` | A JSON body over 1 MiB. |
| 415 | `unsupported_media_type` | A write without `Content-Type: application/json`. |

#### 404: unknown resource, action or dashboard

The UI routes answer with the same short body in every environment. The message
names the kind: `resource`, `action` or `dashboard`. A route looks the name up only
after it has identified the caller and applied `readOnly`, so a signed-out or
refused caller gets the `403` it would get for a name that exists, never this `404`.

```json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "code": "not_found", "message": "action not found" } }
```

Outside production the server console also prints what is registered:

```text
[flowpanel] action not found: "refnud". Registered actions: "refund", "cancel".
```

The JSON CRUD API answers `{ "code": "not_found", "message": "not found" }` for an
unknown route or resource.

## CLI

Every flowpanel command: init, dev, new, migrate, doctor and eject.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/cli

`@flowpanel/cli` sets up, migrates, checks and extends an admin. Start with
`pnpm dlx @flowpanel/cli init`; it installs the CLI as a dev dependency, so later
commands run as `pnpm flowpanel <command>`. The CLI uses the package manager of
your lockfile.

`flowpanel [options] [command]` — Add a typed admin panel to a Next.js app
- `-V, --version` Print the version

`flowpanel init [options]` — Initialize FlowPanel in this project
- `--yes` Accept detected defaults without prompting (CI mode)
- `--dry-run` Print the filesystem plan without writing or installing
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON (implies --yes)
- `--path <path>` Mount the admin at a static path, for example /ops/admin
- `--db <module>` Local module exporting your db or prisma client
- `--schema <module>` Local module exporting your Drizzle schema
- `--auth <module>` Local module exporting getSession(request)
- `--dev-auth` Explicitly use an open development-only admin identity

`flowpanel new [options] <resource>` — Add a resource for a table or model to the admin config
- `<resource>`
- `--table <expr>` The resource's first argument, as code (default: schema.<resource> on Drizzle, the model name on Prisma)
- `--kind <kind>` Adapter kind: drizzle or prisma (default: the config's adapter)
- `--dir <dir>` Write the resource to <dir>/<name>.ts and add it to <dir>/index.ts
- `--hidden` Register the resource without a navigation entry
- `--dry-run` Print the filesystem plan without writing
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON

`flowpanel dev [options]` — Run next dev, plus the queue board when REDIS_URL is set
- `--port <port>` Next.js dev port (default: 3000)
- `--no-board` Skip the queue board (bull-board) even if REDIS_URL is set

`flowpanel migrate [options]` — Apply SQL migrations from flowpanel/migrations/
- `--dry-run` Print migrations that would be applied without running them
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON

`flowpanel doctor [options]` — Check FlowPanel health and wiring
- `--fix` Auto-fix missing route files from templates
- `--dry-run` Show fixes without writing (use with --fix)
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON
- `--path <path>` Resolved admin path when the config uses a dynamic one

`flowpanel eject [options] <target> [name]` — Copy resource <name>, dashboard <path> or layout into your admin folder as code you own
- `<target>`
- `[name]`
- `--force` Overwrite files if they already exist
- `--dry-run` Print the filesystem plan without writing
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON

Every command takes `--help`. Failures exit non-zero; `FLOWPANEL_DEBUG=1` adds the
stack trace. Commands that write build the whole plan first: `--dry-run` prints it,
`--json` returns it for CI, and a failure rolls back earlier writes. A file with
different content is a conflict, never overwritten.

### flowpanel init

`flowpanel init [options]` — Initialize FlowPanel in this project
- `--yes` Accept detected defaults without prompting (CI mode)
- `--dry-run` Print the filesystem plan without writing or installing
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON (implies --yes)
- `--path <path>` Mount the admin at a static path, for example /ops/admin
- `--db <module>` Local module exporting your db or prisma client
- `--schema <module>` Local module exporting your Drizzle schema
- `--auth <module>` Local module exporting getSession(request)
- `--dev-auth` Explicitly use an open development-only admin identity

Detects Next.js, the ORM (Drizzle if both are installed) and the auth helper,
installs `@flowpanel/kit` and `@flowpanel/cli`, and writes the wiring files. In a
terminal it asks for the app name and the paths of the db, schema and auth modules,
shows the plan, and waits for a yes. A module path that does not resolve is asked
again with the reason. When no session helper exists, it also asks whether to write
an open development identity; the answer defaults to no.

```text
┌   FlowPanel init
│
◇  Detected stack ───────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                        │
│  Next.js 16.4.0 · React 19.3.0 · TypeScript · Drizzle  │
│                                                        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
◇  App name, shown as the sidebar brand
│  my-app
│
◇  Drizzle client module, as an import path (exports db)
│  @/db
│
◇  Drizzle schema module, as an import path
│  @/db/schema
│
◇  Session module, as an import path (exports getSession)
│  @/server/lib/auth
│
◇  No session helper found. Use an open development-only admin identity for now?
│  Writes a dev stub that refuses to run in production; replace it with your provider before deploying.
│  Yes
│
●  Admin URL: /admin
│
◇  Filesystem plan ──────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                    │
│  create flowpanel.config.ts                        │
│  create src/app/admin/[[...slug]]/page.tsx         │
│  create src/app/api/flowpanel/[...route]/route.ts  │
│  create src/app/api/flowpanel/stream/route.ts      │
│  create src/styles/admin.css                       │
│  create flowpanel/migrations/0001_init.sql         │
│  create src/server/lib/auth.ts                     │
│  create src/app/admin/layout.tsx                   │
│  create src/app/admin/not-found.tsx                │
│  modify src/app/layout.tsx                         │
│                                                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
◇  Apply these changes?
│  Yes
│
◆  Wrote 10 files
│
◇  Installed @flowpanel/kit@~0.4.0, @flowpanel/cli@~0.4.0
│
▲  src/server/lib/auth.ts signs every request in as an admin in development and throws
│  under `next start`. Replace it with your auth provider before deploying.
│
◇  Next ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                                                │
│  pnpm flowpanel new <table>    add a resource to flowpanel.config.ts                           │
│  pnpm dev                      start Next.js and open the admin URL below                      │
│  pnpm flowpanel migrate        only if you turn on the audit log: creates flowpanel_audit_log  │
│  https://flowpanel.tech/docs/introduction/getting-started                                      │
│                                                                                                │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
└  Admin: http://localhost:3000/admin
```

The closing block names the next commands and the admin URL at the dev server's
default port. The warning above it depends on the session module `init` wrote or
found: the closed stub denies every request until `getSession` returns your
provider's session, or until `pnpm flowpanel init --dev-auth` swaps in the open
development identity.

What varies:

- **`src/`**: in a `src/` project, `app/` and `styles/` paths move under `src/`.
- **Admin mount**: `/admin`, or `/flowpanel` when `/admin` is taken, or
  `--path /ops/admin`. If the fallback is taken too, nothing is written.
- **Admin route**: the catch-all page exports `generateMetadata`, which sets the page
  title from the resource or dashboard, and `not-found.tsx` beside the layout renders
  FlowPanel's not-found page for the admin route. When `next.config` turns on
  `cacheComponents`, the page also exports `instant = false`, so `next dev` does not
  log "encountered uncached data" on every admin page.
- **Admin layout**: imports the stylesheet and renders `ThemeScript` with the
  `x-nonce` request header. Under a strict `script-src`, your middleware must set
  `x-nonce` and the matching CSP header; FlowPanel does not write that middleware.
  When `next.config` turns on `cacheComponents`, as `create-next-app` does from
  Next.js 16.4, the layout also exports `instant = false`, which lets the admin read
  the request before it renders.
  `init` adds `suppressHydrationWarning` to the root layout's `<html>` tag, or prints
  the edit when it cannot patch the file. Without a root layout, the admin gets its
  own.
- **Authentication**: for `better-auth`, `next-auth`, `@clerk/nextjs` or `lucia`,
  when the auth module exports the provider's instance rather than `getSession`,
  `init` writes `server/lib/flowpanel-session.ts` on the matching
  [preset](/docs/guides/authentication). Otherwise it writes a closed `getSession`
  adapter. `--dev-auth`, or a yes to the wizard question, writes an open development
  identity that warns once per process and refuses to run in production. On an
  initialized project, `--dev-auth` touches only the module the config imports
  `getSession` from: it replaces it while it is still one of `init`'s stubs, after
  `flowpanel new` or any other edit, and asks first in a terminal. A module that
  exports anything else, or whose `getSession` you changed, is your own: `init` stops
  with exit `1` and nothing written, saying what to change instead.
- **Role mapping**: with `init`'s stub the config reads `s?.user.role`. With your
  own `getSession` it reads `user.role` only when it is a string and treats other
  sessions as `"guest"`, so the config compiles for any session type.
- **Migration**: `flowpanel/migrations/0001_init.sql` is written for the project's
  database: PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite, read from the Prisma provider or the Drizzle
  modules. An existing file is kept.
- **Piped output**: without a terminal, `init --yes` prints the files it wrote, the
  install result, every warning and the closing block as plain lines, with no colour
  codes, also under `CI`.
- **Prisma provider**: the config's `provider` comes from the `datasource` in the
  Prisma schema: the literal `schema` in `prisma.config.ts`,
  `package.json#prisma.schema`, `prisma/schema.prisma` or `prisma/schema/`. A provider other
  than `postgresql`, `mysql` or `sqlite` stops `init` with nothing written. When no
  datasource is found, `init` writes `postgresql` and warns.
- **Install**: skipped for packages already in `package.json` and installed. A
  package in `node_modules` but missing from `package.json` is added, so the next
  install does not remove it.
- **Dry run**: `--dry-run` lists the db, schema and session modules it would use, the
  session outcome and the migration dialect, then the plan.

#### When `init` stops

- **Not a Next.js project**: exits `1` with `No Next.js project found in <cwd>`. The
  other commands say the same outside a project root.
- **Neither Drizzle nor Prisma in `package.json`**: exits `1` with the install
  command.
- **No Drizzle client, schema or Prisma client at the guessed paths**: exits `1`
  with a starting file for each and the `--db` and `--schema` flags that point at
  yours.
- **No terminal and no `--yes`, `--dry-run` or `--json`**: exits `1`. Pass `--yes`
  in CI.
- **A failed install**: keeps the files, prints the commands to run by hand, and
  exits `1`. So does an installed `@flowpanel/kit` or `@flowpanel/cli` from another
  minor version.

Re-running `init` keeps `flowpanel.config.ts` (or `.tsx`) and skips matching files, and says
`Already set up; nothing changed.` when there is nothing to write. A conflicting
file stops it with nothing written and every conflicting path listed. `--yes`
accepts detected paths; it never overwrites.

### flowpanel migrate

`flowpanel migrate [options]` — Apply SQL migrations from flowpanel/migrations/
- `--dry-run` Print migrations that would be applied without running them
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON

Applies the SQL files in `flowpanel/migrations/` through your config's adapter,
loading the config with `jiti`.

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel migrate
```

`--dry-run` lists the files without loading the config or connecting, so it cannot
tell which are applied. `--json` returns the pending and applied lists. Applied IDs
live in `_flowpanel_migrations`.

Without `flowpanel.config.ts` it exits `1` and says to run `init`, as `new` does.
Before it connects, it checks the connection variable your database client reads
(usually `DATABASE_URL`): when it is unset or empty, `migrate` exits `1` and says
what to set, so the driver never falls back to `localhost`. It reads the modules
the config imports `db` or `prisma` from, plus the Prisma schema; a variable with a
fallback in code, such as `?? "file:local.db"`, is not required. When the database
cannot be reached, the first line is `Cannot reach the database at
<host>:<port> (<code>). Check DATABASE_URL.` for Drizzle and Prisma alike;
the code is the socket error or Prisma's `P1001`, `P1002` or `P1017`.
`FLOWPANEL_DEBUG=1` adds the failed SQL and the stack trace. Under `--json` the
failure is a JSON document with an `error` field, and `applied` is `false` when
nothing ran.

Migrators are serialized at the database, and a concurrent duplicate is a no-op.
On PostgreSQL and SQLite each file and its marker share one transaction. MySQL
commits DDL implicitly: Drizzle holds an advisory lock and Prisma a claim row that
records where a failed run stopped. See [adapter migrations](/docs/reference/adapters#adapter).
Procedural scripts such as trigger bodies are rejected; run them with your ORM's
own migrations.

Every command reads `.env.local`, then `.env`; shell variables win.

### flowpanel doctor

`flowpanel doctor [options]` — Check FlowPanel health and wiring
- `--fix` Auto-fix missing route files from templates
- `--dry-run` Show fixes without writing (use with --fix)
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON
- `--path <path>` Resolved admin path when the config uses a dynamic one

Runs these checks:

- Next.js 15.5 or newer within 15 or 16, and TypeScript installed
- React and React DOM installed at supported, matching versions, and a supported Node.js
- an ORM the adapters support: Drizzle or Prisma
- `flowpanel.config.ts` (or `flowpanel.config.tsx`) exists; before `init`, this is
  the only check after the prerequisites, and its hint is `pnpm dlx @flowpanel/cli init`
- `@flowpanel/kit` is installed and matches the CLI's minor version
- the admin mount in the config (`paths.admin`) resolves to a static path
- the generated files exist: the API route, the SSE route, the seed migration and
  the catch-all admin page. A missing not-found page is a warning that `--fix` still
  repairs
- only one reachable `@flowpanel/kit` installation across the installed
  dependency graph, including package-local peers and third-party plugins.
  Stale pnpm store entries are ignored; uninstalled projects skip this check
- every ejected admin page still carries its eject marker
- with `cacheComponents` on: Next.js 16.3 or newer, no `runtime`, `dynamic`,
  `revalidate` or `fetchCache` export in the generated routes and admin page, and
  `instant = false` in the catch-all admin page and in an admin layout that reads the
  request. `--fix` adds it to a catch-all page `init` wrote; a page you edited gets
  the hint only
- `tsc --noEmit` passes. When `.next/types` is missing, `doctor` runs `next typegen`
  first, so the route and layout types Next generates exist. When `next typegen`
  fails, the `tsc` hint shows its error first, then what `tsc` reported
- `flowpanel.config.ts` evaluates; an error there is a failure with the error as
  its hint. With a `.tsx` config, this check and the one above name that file

More checks warn without failing the run: a session module that is still the
closed stub (`getSession` returns `null`) or the open development identity from
`init --dev-auth`, an empty `resources` array, a missing `DATABASE_URL` while
`flowpanel/migrations/` holds SQL files, an audit table from 0.3 that lacks the 0.4
columns (`--fix` writes the `0002` migration), and, with `DATABASE_URL` set, a
resource whose table the database does not have, counted through the config's adapter. A warning prints as a yellow `!` line and
carries `"warn": true` in `--json`. A check that crashes is a warning too, with
`Could not check:` and the first line of the error as its hint.

When no `eslint.config.*` in the project, or above it up to the repository or
workspace root, loads `@flowpanel/eslint-plugin`, `doctor` adds a note
(a `·` line, `"info": true` in `--json`) that suggests the
[ESLint plugin](/docs/reference/eslint-plugin); its `audit-row-action-needs-confirm`
rule flags a destructive action without a `confirm`. A note never fails the run or
counts as a warning. In `--json`, `hint` appears on failing checks, warnings and
notes only.

Mount checks follow route groups, parallel slots and intercepting routes.

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel doctor
$ pnpm flowpanel doctor --fix
$ pnpm flowpanel doctor --fix --dry-run
```

`--fix` recreates missing generated files from the `init` templates, checks the files
again, then generates types and runs `tsc` once, so one run ends green when the files
were all that was missing. Other failures print a hint. A failed check exits non-zero, so it can run in CI.

### flowpanel eject

`flowpanel eject [options] <target> [name]` — Copy resource <name>, dashboard <path> or layout into your admin folder as code you own
- `<target>`
- `[name]`
- `--force` Overwrite files if they already exist
- `--dry-run` Print the filesystem plan without writing
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON

Ejects a `resource`, `dashboard` or `layout` into your repo. See
[Eject to source](/docs/customization/eject).

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel eject resource users
$ pnpm flowpanel eject dashboard "/monitoring"
$ pnpm flowpanel eject layout
```

It writes the files under the admin mount, as one transaction. An ejected resource
stays in the config, because the ejected `actions.ts` reads rows through it; an ejected
dashboard's entry is commented out. When a target file exists, the plan is printed with
`Use --force to overwrite.`: a dry run exits `0` and a real run exits `1`. `--force`
replaces existing files. It follows a re-exporting root config and a `new --dir`
resources directory.

### flowpanel dev

`flowpanel dev [options]` — Run next dev, plus the queue board when REDIS_URL is set
- `--port <port>` Next.js dev port (default: 3000)
- `--no-board` Skip the queue board (bull-board) even if REDIS_URL is set

Runs `next dev`, plus the queue board (bull-board) when `scripts/board-server.mts`
(or `.ts`) exists and `REDIS_URL` is set. It runs the `next` binary installed in the
project with Node and never downloads one. A Yarn PnP project gets the message that
says how to set `nodeLinker` to `node-modules`. A busy port stops it with `Port <n> is in use. Pass --port
<other>.`

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel dev --port 3000
```

A port counts as busy when anything answers on `127.0.0.1` or `::1`.
Output is prefixed `[next]` and `[board]`; when Next.js is ready, `dev` prints the
admin URL. When one process exits, both stop.
`--no-board` skips the queue board. The board runs with `tsx` from your project, so
install it as a dev dependency (`pnpm add -D tsx`) when you use queues.

### flowpanel new

`flowpanel new [options] <resource>` — Add a resource for a table or model to the admin config
- `<resource>`
- `--table <expr>` The resource's first argument, as code (default: schema.<resource> on Drizzle, the model name on Prisma)
- `--kind <kind>` Adapter kind: drizzle or prisma (default: the config's adapter)
- `--dir <dir>` Write the resource to <dir>/<name>.ts and add it to <dir>/index.ts
- `--hidden` Register the resource without a navigation entry
- `--dry-run` Print the filesystem plan without writing
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON

Adds a resource to the config, or as its own file with `--dir`.

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel new posts
```

```text
└  Added resource "posts" to flowpanel.config.ts
```

It reads the table from your schema and adds an entry with its columns, search
fields, filters and default sort to the `resources` array, chosen the same way as
`--dir` below; an enum column gets a `select` filter. It also adds `resource` to the
`@flowpanel/kit` import when missing and removes the placeholder comment that `init`
wrote above the array. It checks the schema has the table, by SQL name or export
name, and exits `1` if not, or if the resource exists. It follows a root config that
re-exports another module, and when the config reads a `--dir` directory, `new`
writes there. `--hidden` without `--dir` adds `hidden: true` to the entry.

On Prisma it reads `schema.prisma`: `new users` resolves to the model mapped to
that table (`User`), and an unknown name exits `1` with the list of models. The
entry gets `name` set to the `@@map` table name, or the model in plural snake case
(`OrderItem` becomes `order_items`), so the URL and navigation read like a Drizzle
table's. A relation field becomes a `reference` when the target model already has a
resource. The model is added to `FlowpanelResources` under that name, so its rows and
the references to it are typed.

#### One file per resource

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel new user_visit --dir admin/config/resources --hidden
```

`--dir` reads the Drizzle schema and writes `admin/config/resources/user-visit.ts`:

```ts
import { enumOf, resource } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import * as schema from "@/db/schema";

const Surface = enumOf(schema.activitySurface.enumValues, { web: "Web", tma: "Tma" });

export const userVisit = resource(schema.userVisit, {
  hidden: true,
  columns: [
    "id",
    { field: "userId", label: "User", reference: { resource: "user", labelField: "email" } },
    { field: "surface", format: Surface.format },
    { field: "startedAt", format: { kind: "date", time: true } },
    "touches",
  ],
  filters: [{ field: "surface", type: "select" }],
  defaultSort: { field: "startedAt", dir: "desc" },
});
```

and adds it to `admin/config/resources/index.ts`. The first time, it also imports
that directory's `resources` into `flowpanel.config.ts` and spreads it into the
array; when the config is shaped differently it prints the line to add. Columns are chosen by type; an
enum gets an `enumOf` stub; an integer column whose name ends in `Cents` or `_cents`
shows as money, `format: { kind: "money", minorUnits: 2 }`; a foreign key becomes a `reference` labelled by the
target's `name`, `title` or `email` when the target already has a file, which
also makes it a searchable picker in the generated create and edit forms, so
scaffold referenced tables first. JSON and long text are left out of the list columns, `name`,
`title` and `email` become search fields, and the list sorts by `createdAt` or `startedAt`.
`--hidden` keeps the resource out of the navigation.

Re-running changes nothing; a different existing file stops it. `--dir` is
Drizzle only. Without `--dir`, a config whose `resources` comes from a `--dir`
directory gets the new file there; any other `resources` that is not an array
literal is left unchanged, and `new` exits `1`.

`--table <expr>` sets the table expression, skips the schema check and writes empty
options. `--kind` defaults to the adapter the config builds.

## Testing

Walk every admin page in one Playwright call, and unit-test widgets and record headers over rows you pass.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/testing

Documented types: smokeAdmin, SmokeAdminOptions, SmokeAdminReport, A11yViolation, widgetContext, WidgetContextOptions, headerContext

`@flowpanel/kit/test` holds `smokeAdmin`, which walks a running admin in
Playwright and fails on a broken page; `@flowpanel/kit/test/widgets` unit-tests a
widget over rows you pass. Playwright is an optional peer of the kit, so install
it as a dev dependency; no other kit subpath loads it.

```sh
pnpm add -D @playwright/test @axe-core/playwright
pnpm exec playwright install chromium
```

`@axe-core/playwright` runs the accessibility checks: with `a11y: true` and no `@axe-core/playwright`, `smokeAdmin` fails and names the package to install.

### smokeAdmin

```ts
import { test } from "@playwright/test";
import { smokeAdmin } from "@flowpanel/kit/test";

test("the admin is healthy", async ({ page }) => {
  await smokeAdmin(page, { paths: { admin: "/admin" }, a11y: true });
});
```

The walk starts at `paths.admin`, opens every dashboard and list in the navigation,
then opens each list's first row as its record page or drawer. On a record page it
opens every other tab as `?tab=<key>` (`tabs: false` skips them), so a failure
names its URL, such as `/admin/users/1?tab=activity`. A drawer is checked on its first tab.

### What it asserts

| Assertion | How it fails |
| --- | --- |
| Every navigation answers below 400 | `<route>: responded 500` |
| Nothing wrote to `console.error` | `console.error: <text>` |
| No page rendered `[data-fp-error]` | `<route>: rendered a FlowPanel error surface` |
| Zero WCAG 2.2 AA violations, with `a11y` | `<route>: axe <rule> (<impact>)` |
| The navigation has at least one route | `smokeAdmin found no navigation under <paths.admin> …` |

`[data-fp-error]` marks FlowPanel's error cards: a failed widget, a failed read, a
failed drawer. A walk that finds no routes fails. Pages count as loaded when `main`
is visible, since realtime pages never reach network idle.

### Options and report

`SmokeAdminOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `paths?` | `{ admin?: string }` | Where the admin is mounted: the config's `paths.admin`. Default: `"/admin"`. |
| `cookie?` | `{ name: string; value: string; domain?: string }` | Session cookie added before the walk, for an admin behind authentication. |
| `resources?` | `string[]` | Restrict the walk to these nav segments — `"customers"` for `/admin/customers`. Every entry visited when omitted. |
| `a11y?` | `boolean` | Run axe against every visited route. Needs `@axe-core/playwright`; without it `smokeAdmin` fails and names the package. Default: `false`. |
| `maxRows?` | `number` | How many rows of each list the walk opens. Default: `1`. |
| `tabs?` | `boolean` | On each record page, open every other detail tab as `?tab=<key>` and check it the same way. Default: `true`. |

`SmokeAdminReport`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `visited` | `string[]` | Every route the walk loaded, in order, including rows it opened. |
| `consoleErrors` | `string[]` |  |
| `a11yViolations` | `A11yViolation[]` |  |

`A11yViolation`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `route` | `string` |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |
| `impact?` | `string` |  |

`smokeAdmin` resolves with the report, or throws an `Error` listing each problem
and the report as JSON.

```ts
import { test } from "@playwright/test";
import { smokeAdmin } from "@flowpanel/kit/test";

test("the admin is healthy", async ({ page }) => {
  const report = await smokeAdmin(page, {
    paths: { admin: "/admin" },
    cookie: { name: "session", value: process.env.E2E_SESSION ?? "" },
    resources: ["/", "customers", "orders"],
    maxRows: 3,
    a11y: true,
  });
  console.log(`${report.visited.length} routes visited`);
});
```

`resources` takes nav segments: `"/"` is the landing dashboard, `"customers"` is
`/admin/customers`. `cookie` is set on the admin's origin unless it has a `domain`.

### Unit-test a widget

`widgetContext` builds a widget context over rows you pass instead of a database.
`resolveWidget` runs the widget as a dashboard does and returns its card's props.

```ts
import { resolveWidget, widgetContext } from "@flowpanel/kit/test/widgets";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { paidToday } from "@/admin/config/dashboards/money";

it("counts only today's paid invoices", async () => {
  const ctx = widgetContext({
    rows: {
      invoices: [
        { status: "paid", paidAt: new Date("2026-09-25T09:00:00Z") },
        { status: "paid", paidAt: new Date("2026-09-24T09:00:00Z") },
      ],
    },
    range: { from: new Date("2026-09-25T00:00:00Z"), to: new Date("2026-09-25T23:59:59Z") },
  });
  const { props } = await resolveWidget(paidToday, ctx);
  expect(props.value).toBe(1);
  expect(props.drilldown).toContain("/admin/invoices?f_status=paid");
});
```

`ctx.count`, `ctx.read`, `compare` and `ctx.link` run as in the admin. Without
`admin`, each key of `rows` is a resource whose columns are its rows' keys. Pass
`admin`, your `defineAdmin` config, when the widget needs views, dashboards or
references. Access rules apply, so pass `session` and `role`; tenant scope does not.

`sql` answers `ctx.sql`: rows, or a function of the statement and values. `row` and
`resource` make a record-page context. `filters` sets `ctx.filters`.

`WidgetContextOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rows?` | `Readonly<Record<string, readonly Row[]>>` | Rows per resource name. `ctx.count`, `ctx.read`, `compare` and count metrics read them. |
| `admin?` | `ResolvedAdminConfig` | Your `defineAdmin` config, with only its database replaced by `rows`; carries no tenant scope. Without `admin`, every key of `rows` is a resource whose columns are the keys its rows carry. |
| `row?` | `Row` | The viewed record, for a record-page widget: `ctx.row`, `ctx.id` and `ctx.rowOf`. |
| `resource?` | `string` | The resource `row` belongs to; `ctx.rowOf` of another name throws. |
| `range?` | `{ from: Date; to: Date }` | The picked period; `compare` reads the one before it. Default: `the whole history until now`. |
| `filters?` | `Readonly<Record<string, string>>` | The dashboard filters widgets read as `ctx.filters`. Default: `{}`. |
| `sql?` | `SqlAnswer` | Rows every `ctx.sql` returns, or a function given the statement (`$1…$n`) and its values. |
| `db?` | `unknown` | Handed to widgets as `ctx.db`. Default: `null`. |
| `session?` | `Session \| null` | Default: `null`. |
| `role?` | `string` | The role access checks compare. Default: `"admin"`. |
| `formatting?` | `FormattingConfig` | Without `admin`: locale, zone and currency, as `defineAdmin` takes them. |
| `labels?` | `LabelsConfig` | Without `admin`: overrides of the admin's strings. |
| `paths?` | `{ admin?: string }` | Without `admin`: where the admin is mounted, as `defineAdmin` takes `paths`. Default: ``{ admin: "/admin" }``. |

`headerContext` builds the second argument of `detail.title`, `subtitle` and
`badge`:

```ts
import { headerContext } from "@flowpanel/kit/test/widgets";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import admin from "@/admin/config";
import { customerCard } from "@/admin/config/resources/customer-card";

it("says how long the customer has been with us", () => {
  const ctx = headerContext({ admin });
  const row = {
    id: 1,
    email: "ops@northwind.example",
    name: "Ada",
    company: "Northwind Audio",
    plan: "pro",
    status: "active",
    mrr: 4900,
    churned: false,
    createdAt: new Date("2026-01-05"),
    lastSeenAt: null,
    deletedAt: null,
  } as const;
  expect(customerCard.subtitle(row, ctx)).toContain("Customer since");
});
```

`@flowpanel/kit/test/widgets` is ESM-only; `@flowpanel/kit/test` also loads with `require`, for Playwright projects compiled to CommonJS.

#### Run it in Vitest

Inline FlowPanel's packages, or the run fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for
`next/cache`, and alias `@/`, since Vitest does not read `tsconfig.json` paths:

```ts
// vitest.config.ts
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config";

export default defineConfig({
  resolve: { alias: { "@": fileURLToPath(new URL(".", import.meta.url)) } },
  test: { server: { deps: { inline: [/@flowpanel\//] } } },
});
```

### Playwright config

`smokeAdmin` calls `page.goto(paths.admin)`, so set a `baseURL` and a `webServer`:

```ts
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "@playwright/test";

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "./e2e",
  use: { baseURL: "http://localhost:3000" },
  webServer: { command: "pnpm dev", url: "http://localhost:3000", reuseExistingServer: true },
});
```

The test user needs the role your admin requires.

### Authentication

`cookie` suits a bare session token your own code issues. For better-auth,
next-auth and other providers that sign sessions, sign in first; `smokeAdmin` reuses
the page's context. Wait until the sign-in page has redirected, or the redirect
aborts the walk's first navigation with `net::ERR_ABORTED`.

```ts
import { test } from "@playwright/test";
import { smokeAdmin } from "@flowpanel/kit/test";

test("the admin is healthy", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/login");
  await page.getByLabel("Email").fill("admin@example.com");
  await page.getByLabel("Password").fill(process.env.E2E_PASSWORD ?? "");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in" }).click();
  await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname !== "/login");

  await smokeAdmin(page);
});
```

## ESLint plugin

Five rules that catch config mistakes the type system cannot.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/eslint-plugin

`@flowpanel/eslint-plugin` is an optional package that catches mistakes type-checking
misses: server code imported into a client component, a destructive action without
a confirm, duplicate resource names. Rule names are stable; options and messages
may change before 1.0.

### Install

```bash
pnpm add -D @flowpanel/eslint-plugin
```

It needs `eslint >= 8`; the config is flat config.

### Setup

```ts
import flowpanel from "@flowpanel/eslint-plugin";

export default [flowpanel.configs.recommended];
```

`configs.recommended` turns on all five rules. To choose them yourself:

```ts
import flowpanel from "@flowpanel/eslint-plugin";

export default [
  {
    plugins: { flowpanel },
    rules: {
      "flowpanel/prefer-shorthand-filter": "warn",
      "flowpanel/audit-row-action-needs-confirm": "error",
      "flowpanel/no-server-import-in-client": "error",
      "flowpanel/require-unique-resource-names": "error",
      "flowpanel/no-typo-column-keyword": "warn",
    },
  },
];
```

### The rules

| Rule | Recommended | Type | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`no-server-import-in-client`](#no-server-import-in-client) | `error` | problem | no |
| [`audit-row-action-needs-confirm`](#audit-row-action-needs-confirm) | `error` | problem | no |
| [`require-unique-resource-names`](#require-unique-resource-names) | `error` | problem | no |
| [`prefer-shorthand-filter`](#prefer-shorthand-filter) | `warn` | suggestion | yes |
| [`no-typo-column-keyword`](#no-typo-column-keyword) | `warn` | problem | no |

#### `no-server-import-in-client`

In a `"use client"` file, flags imports of:

- `server-only` and any `*/server-only` specifier;
- any specifier with a `/server` segment, such as `@/server/lib/auth` or
  `react-dom/server`, except `next/server`;
- an app-local path (`@/`, `~/`, `./`, `../`, `src/`) with a `db` segment, such as
  `@/db` or `../lib/db/client`.

`import type` is ignored.

#### `audit-row-action-needs-confirm`

Flags an `actions` or `bulkActions` entry with `variant: "destructive"` and no
`confirm`.

```ts fragment
// bad
actions: [{ key: "delete", label: "Delete", variant: "destructive", run }];

// good
actions: [
  {
    key: "delete",
    label: "Delete",
    variant: "destructive",
    confirm: "Are you sure?",
    run,
  },
];
```

#### `require-unique-resource-names`

Flags two `resource()` entries in one `defineAdmin` with the same name, read from a
literal `options.name` or a string ref. Identifiers resolve through a
`const x = resource(…)` in the same file; the same unresolved identifier listed
twice is flagged too.

#### `prefer-shorthand-filter`

Rewrites filter `options` whose every `label` equals its `value` as plain strings.
Autofixable.

```ts
// bad
filters: [
  {
    field: "status",
    type: "select",
    options: [
      { label: "active", value: "active" },
      { label: "archived", value: "archived" },
    ],
  },
];

// good
filters: [{ field: "status", type: "select", options: ["active", "archived"] }];
```

#### `no-typo-column-keyword`

Flags `userid`, `createdat`, `updatedat` and `isactive`, in any casing other than
the camelCase one, in `columns`. The rule reads the source only, so it also catches
them where the rows are untyped. Not autofixable.
